description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Location: Washington, D.C Metro, Boston, MA or Remote, US - Eastern, Central U.S. timezones
Travel: Up to 25%, domestic or international
Job ID: 1956

The Role:

We are seeking a Sr. PBP Director, GTM to lead People Business Partner support for IonQ's global Go-To-Market organization.

This leader will serve as the primary People partner to the global GTM organization, including the Chief Business Officer and their leadership team, working closely across sales, marketing, customer success, field engineering, revenue operations, and other commercial functions to translate business priorities into people and organizational strategies that drive growth and performance.

This is a highly visible, hands-on role at a pivotal moment for IonQ's commercial growth. You'll play a central role in scaling a high-performing sales and GTM culture, elevating the talent and organizational foundations this fast-growing, geographically distributed team needs, and proving out a PBP model that can expand as the org does.

The ideal candidate combines strong business and sales HR acumen and executive presence with a pragmatic, roll-up-your-sleeves approach. They will enjoy operating the fast moving and “bias to action” culture of GTM, and be a true business partner. They’re a highly collaborative driver with a firm and flexible point of view on how to accelerate the business via strategic and operationally excellent people solutions.

Responsibilities:

Partner with the Business

  • Serve as the senior People advisor to GTM leadership, building trusted relationships and providing counsel on organizational effectiveness, talent, workforce planning, leadership, and culture.
  • Translate GTM's commercial strategy and revenue priorities into practical people strategies that support pipeline growth, sales productivity, and go-to-market execution.
  • Build a deep understanding of IonQ's commercial motion — sales segments, quota structures, territory design, and buyer landscape — to proactively identify organizational opportunities and risks.
  • Coach senior leaders through complex organizational, talent, performance, and leadership decisions.

Build the PBP Function for GTM

  • Design a PBP model and coverage plan appropriate to a fast-growing, quota-carrying commercial organization, with a clear point of view on when and how to add headcount as the org grows.
  • Partner with Sales Compensation and Total Rewards so GTM's comp and rewards programs - plan design, quota-setting support, leveling and offer governance - are fit for purpose in a fast-growing commercial organization.
  • Act as the voice of the business with Talent Acquisition on GTM hiring: translate the growth plan into a workforce plan and role requirements, hold hiring managers to a consistent bar and a disciplined process, and feed quality-of-hire and ramp signals back into the profiles we recruit against.
  • Partner with managers and enable onboarding and ramp, with a point of view on what's driving time to full productivity and what needs to change.
  • Serve as execution partner for enterprise-wide People practices across GTM - performance management cycle, annual compensation review, and engagement survey cycle.
  • As the team expands, hire, develop, and set clear priorities and performance expectations for the PBPs who join.

Lead Organization Design & Change

  • Lead organizational design initiatives across GTM, including territory and coverage models, team structures, leadership accountabilities, and workforce planning.
  • Guide leaders and the organization through growth, restructuring, and evolving go-to-market priorities.
  • Balance enterprise-wide consistency with the unique needs of a commercial, revenue-driven organization.

Drive Talent & Organizational Performance

  • Own talent outcomes across GTM, with particular focus on seller retention, ramp-time, succession, leadership effectiveness, and performance.
  • Build robust talent and succession plans, identify capability gaps across the sales leadership bench, and partner with leaders to strengthen it.
  • Coach leaders on performance management, feedback, seller development, and difficult people decisions, including performance-based exits common in a quota-driven environment.
  • Use people and sales performance data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and translate them into action.
  • Strengthen employee engagement, organizational health, and a high-performance culture aligned with IonQ's values.

Requirements:

  • 12+ years of progressive HR/People experience, including significant senior HR Business Partner leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering directly with senior sales, marketing, or commercial leadership teams.
  • Hands-on involvement in annual comp planning alongside Finance and Sales Ops, including quota setting and plan changes.
  • Experience supporting quota-carrying, revenue-focused, or commercial/GTM organizations.
  • Experience supporting a business through significant commercial scaling, market expansion, or transformation, including acquisition integration.
  • Strong business acumen and demonstrated ability to connect people strategy directly to revenue and commercial outcomes.
  • Proven expertise in organizational design, talent management, succession planning, leadership coaching, and change management.
  • Experience operating as a function of one or close to it, including a clear point of view on prioritization and what you deliberately chose not to do.
  • Strong executive presence, judgment, and the ability to influence and challenge senior leaders constructively.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, ambiguous, high-growth environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience building a PBP or HRBP function from the ground up, including a track record of scaling from individual contributor to team leader.
  • Experience supporting global or internationally distributed sales organizations (EMEA, public sector/federal, or emerging markets).
  • Experience with sales compensation design, territory planning, or quota methodology.
  • Experience working within a high-growth technology or deep-tech company.

What Success Looks Like:

Within the first 6–12 months, this leader will have:

  • Established themselves as a trusted, high-impact partner to GTM leadership.
  • Proven the value of dedicated PBP support for GTM, building the case (and the plan) for additional PBP headcount as the org scales.
  • Created greater clarity around GTM's organizational structure, leadership accountabilities, and critical talent.
  • Strengthened succession and talent plans across the sales and GTM leadership bench.
  • Delivered measurable progress on seller retention, ramp-time, engagement, and leadership effectiveness.
  • Partnered effectively with Sales Compensation and Total Rewards to ensure GTM's comp and incentive programs support desired seller behavior.
  • Accelerated cultural alignment and adoption of IonQ's values and ways of working across a fast-scaling commercial team.

The total compensation package includes base, bonus, equity, and a range of benefit options found on our career site.

title: Senior Data Engineer - Analytics
excerpt: Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country.
description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

As a Senior Data Engineer (Analytics) you own the layer where messy operational data becomes a number a business leader will act on. You’ll sit with the people who run our business, learn how the work actually happens, and turn that into certified models, metric definitions that survive scrutiny, and reports people use. Our analytics warehouse unifies four platforms into one measurement model across dozens of unique client workflows.

This is a data modeling and measurement enabling role more than a pipeline development role, though such skills will be helpful. Expect real time on calls with finance, operations, and client-facing teams, and real time in dbt, SQL, and Power BI. If you won’t ship a dashboard you can’t reconcile, you’ll fit in great.

What You’ll Do

  • Run discovery with business stakeholders. Find the real need behind the request and turn it into acceptance criteria you can build against.
  • Model noisy healthcare operational data into certified dimensional models across our Databricks bronze → silver → gold architecture in dbt and SQL. Our sources disagree with each other in ways that are interesting rather than trivial. Sorting that out is most of the job.
  • Own metric definitions. One measure, one definition, one place, documented so a non-engineer can read it. Today a single operating metric can be re-derived in a dozen models; collapsing that into a governed semantic layer is yours.
  • Build and own the visualization layer. Power BI semantic models, dashboards, and paginated reports, including refresh health and semantic-model currency. We want real visualization judgment: the right chart for the question, a hierarchy an executive can read in ten seconds, and a reason for every choice.
  • Own observability for your models. Freshness and latency detection, statistical anomaly detection, and value-drift monitoring, plus the data tests, regression guards, and CI checks that keep a defect you just fixed from coming back.
  • Own orchestration for what you build. dbt Cloud job design, Airflow DAGs, scheduling, dependency ordering, dependable incremental runs.
  • Write it down. Design documents, model documentation, a CI-enforced knowledge base, and business-readable handoff packets, so whoever inherits your work doesn’t have to re-derive it.
  • Automate the recurring work. We codify repeating work into repeatable, testable, AI-assisted workflows instead of checklists in someone’s notes. You should be comfortable directing LLMs and supervising what they produce.

What You Bring

  • 6+ years across analytics engineering, BI engineering, data engineering, or business analysis, with production ownership of the models and metrics you built.
  • Expert SQL and strong dimensional modeling instincts. You spot a grain mismatch in someone else’s model before you run it.
  • Production dbt: models, tests, macros, exposures, documentation, and CI. You have opinions about project structure and can defend them.
  • Hands-on with a cloud lakehouse or warehouse. Databricks and Spark SQL preferred; Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift transfer well.
  • Real visualization talent. You’ve owned a BI semantic layer and the reports on top of it, not just the tables underneath. Power BI and DAX strongly preferred; Looker/LookML, Tableau, MetricFlow, or Cube are credible substitutes. Bring dashboards you designed and be ready to say what you left out.
  • Stakeholder fluency. You can run a requirements conversation with a non-technical owner, turn a vague complaint into a testable definition, explain a data problem as business risk, and tell someone their metric is wrong without losing them.
  • A reconciliation reflex. When two numbers disagree you don’t average them, escalate them, or trust the newer one. You find out why.
  • Git and pull-request discipline as normal practice rather than overhead.
  • Python where it’s genuinely the right tool (API calls, file parsing, statistics, report generation), and the judgment to reach for SQL where it isn’t.
  • Comfort with high autonomy in a fast, async, Slack-first environment. You decide inside your lane and inform, rather than queuing decisions for permission.
  • Strong writing. Much of your impact is a document, a definition, or a chart someone reads without you in the room.

Bonus points for

  • Healthcare data: claims (837/835/UB04), DRG and coding review, payment integrity, provider contracts, or revenue cycle.
  • Data contracts, schema enforcement, or ODCS-style governance; quality gating in CI.
  • Databricks Unity Catalog, lineage, and cost/DBU accountability.
  • Paginated reporting, SharePoint/Excel delivery, or other “the business needs it in exactly this format” surfaces.
  • Working alongside AI coding agents and reviewing what they produce against a contract you wrote.

Why Join Us

  • Own a real greenfield problem. We’re building a governed semantic layer that centralizes business logic. It’s a funded priority and one of the highest-impact problems on the team.
  • Strong engineering foundation. We already have 634 production models, 1,800+ automated tests, and strong CI guardrails. You can focus on solving new problems instead of building basic engineering discipline from scratch.
  • See your work reach the business. This team owns the work all the way to the reporting layer, so you’ll see how your decisions affect real business users.
  • Work directly with stakeholders. Every project has a clear business owner and defined acceptance criteria, so you know who you’re building for and what success looks like.
  • Use AI in the actual engineering workflow. We’ve built agent-driven workflows into our day-to-day development process, and our delivery velocity has grown significantly as a result. If you’re interested in actually using AI to change how software gets built, you’ll have plenty of opportunity here.
  • Make an impact in healthcare. The systems you build help a large-scale healthcare payment integrity business understand and improve its performance.

What We Offer

  • Work from anywhere in the US! Machinify is digital-first.
  • Full Medical/Dental/Vision for employees & their families
  • Flexible and trusting environment where you’ll feel empowered to do your best work
  • Unlimited FTO
  • Competitive salary, equity, 401(k) including employer match

The salary for this position is based on an array of factors unique to each candidate: Such as years and depth of experience, set skills, certifications, etc. We are hiring for different levels, and our Recruiting team will let you know if you qualify for a different role/range. Salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes meaningful equity, excellent healthcare, flexible time off, and other benefits and perks.

Pay range: $170,000 - $200,000

description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

As a Staff Data Engineer on the Migrations team, you are the end-to-end technical and operational owner of client migrations. You will drive the full lifecycle, from deep-dive legacy analysis to production deployment, while orchestrating collaboration across Operations, Client Success, Product, Data Science and Platform Engineering. You don't just implement; you own the outcome.

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role for someone who can think like an architect, execute like a senior engineer, and coordinate like a program manager — all on the same project. You'll own the problem space from discovery to go-live, making the defining architectural decisions and writing the code that brings them to life.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead discovery & technical due diligence — get to the bottom of poorly documented legacy systems (ETL, stored procedures, reporting layers, file feeds), reconstruct the business logic, and capture it in the lineage maps, mapping specs, and risk analyses everyone builds from.
  • Reverse-engineer complex legacy systems using agents— you will be responsible for reverse-engineering complex, undocumented legacy systems (SSIS packages, stored procedures) where business logic is embedded, not documented. You must be able to reconstruct the intent of these systems to build modern, stable equivalents.
  • Drive ambiguity to resolution — spot the unknowns early, own the open questions, and pull answers from clients, SMEs, and Operations instead of waiting to be unblocked.
  • Architect & build the migration pipelines — turn intricate legacy logic into production-grade Airflow DAGs and Spark jobs on the Machinify platform, edge cases, payer-specific carve-outs, and business-rule exceptions included, owning the full flow from ingestion through reconciliation to steady-state handoff.
  • Make and document the hard architectural calls — own the decisions that matter (pipeline design, partitioning strategy, validation approach) and leave a clear trail of the reasoning so others can learn from and build on it.
  • Prove correctness at scale — build automated reconciliation frameworks that confirm, with confidence, that migrated output matches the source down to the row.
  • Own the program end to end — be the single technical owner from kickoff through go-live and hypercare: scope, sequence, and track the work, surface risks before they bite, align Operations, Client Success, Platform Engineering, SMEs, and the client, and drive UAT through to sign-off.
  • Raise the bar for the practice — Institutionalize migration knowledge by codifying runbooks and retrospectives, mentor L3/L4 engineers to build independent capability, and turn recurring migration pain points into scalable, reusable tooling.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years as a hands-on Data Engineer or Software Engineer, with demonstrated experience independently owning complex, multi-stakeholder technical projects from start to finish.
  • Strong Python and SQL — fluent with complex, unfamiliar legacy code, not just greenfield work.
  • Apache Spark — deep understanding of distributed processing, performance tuning, partitioning, and debugging at scale.
  • Apache Airflow — advanced; comfortable designing and authoring production DAG architectures from scratch.
  • AI-assisted development — actively uses coding agents (Claude, Copilot, Cursor, or equivalent) as a force multiplier in daily engineering work. Comfortable prompt-engineering for code generation, debugging, and documentation, and able to evaluate and trust AI output critically.
  • Legacy ETL stack — able to reconstruct intent from code and translate it faithfully into a modern stack (e.g., From SSIS, SQL Server stored procedures, T-SQL, or equivalent).
  • Data validation & reconciliation at scale — experience designing automated frameworks that prove migrated data matches source systems with high confidence.
  • AWS — proficient with S3, solid grasp of cloud-native data patterns such as partitioned object storage, secure cross-account access, and cost/performance trade-offs.
  • Cross-functional coordination — proven ability to drive alignment across engineering, operations, and client-facing teams simultaneously, without losing velocity.
  • Clear technical communication — able to write discovery specs, architecture docs, and stakeholder updates that are accurate, concise, and actionable for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Data-first mindset & fidelity — a rigorous, data-first mindset, with deep experience in building automated reconciliation frameworks that guarantee 100% data fidelity between legacy and modern systems.

🌱 Why Join Us

  • Full ownership — you own the whole arc of a migration, from first look to go-live. No fragmented handoffs — just the autonomy and context to do it well.
  • Immediate business impact — every migration you land enables a health plan to process claims more accurately and efficiently.
  • Technical depth + breadth — you'll work across legacy systems, modern orchestration, distributed compute, cloud infra, and client-facing delivery in every project.
  • Pivotal moment — we're scaling the migrations capability for a fast-growing platform; the standards and patterns you set will shape how dozens of future migrations run

What We Offer

  • Work from anywhere in the US! Machinify is digital-first.
  • Full Medical/Dental/Vision for employees & their families
  • Flexible and trusting environment where you’ll feel empowered to do your best work
  • Unlimited FTO
  • Competitive salary, equity, 401(k) including employer match

The salary for this position is based on an array of factors unique to each candidate: Such as years and depth of experience, set skills, certifications, etc. The base salary range for this role is $230k-$260k. We are hiring for different levels, and our Recruiting team will let you know if you qualify for a different role/range. Salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes meaningful equity, excellent healthcare, flexible time off, and other benefits and perks.

excerpt: About Cordatus Cordatus Resource Group is a business operations consulting firm serving mid-market and PE-backed companies.
description:
About Cordatus

Cordatus Resource Group is a business operations consulting firm serving mid-market and PE-backed companies. We work process first, people second: we redesign how work gets done, then automate it or staff it with specialist talent. We've delivered $325M+ in business value for our clients. Our automation practice builds outbound and revenue systems for companies that need more than a template campaign.

The Role

You'll design, pitch, and build custom outbound systems for our clients. Every client is different. One might be a PE-backed services firm prospecting into CFOs. Another might be a staffing company running high-volume multichannel outreach, or a niche B2B firm that needs signal-based targeting. You'll figure out what will generate pipeline for each one, make the case for it, and then build it and run it.

This role is half consultant, half engineer. You'll be on client calls bringing ideas the client hasn't considered, and then you'll be the one who ships them. If you only want to build, or only want to advise, this isn't the right fit.

What You'll Do

  • Run discovery with clients to understand their ICP, offer, sales motion, and what they've already tried
  • Propose new outreach strategies and campaign concepts, and explain the expected impact in business terms
  • Build enrichment, scoring, and personalization workflows in Clay, including waterfall enrichment, signal detection (hiring, funding, tech stack changes, leadership moves), AI research and copy columns, and custom HTTP API integrations
  • Build and manage multichannel sequences (email and LinkedIn) in La Growth Machine
  • Build and maintain the workflows that connect the stack in n8n (our primary automation platform, with some Make.com), syncing Clay and LGM with client CRMs such as HubSpot through webhooks and APIs, including unsubscribe and suppression handling
  • Own deliverability for your campaigns: domain and inbox setup, warmup, sending limits, and monitoring
  • Track results, diagnose what isn't working, and iterate quickly
  • Turn one-off builds into reusable templates, Clay tables, and n8n workflows so each new client launches faster
  • Manage 3-5 client accounts at once, with clear timelines and proactive communication

What You Bring

Required

  • 2+ years building outbound automation, with advanced Clay experience (beyond templates): HTTP API calls, formulas, conditional runs, and AI columns with structured prompts
  • Hands-on multichannel outbound experience in LGM or a comparable tool (HeyReach, Lemlist, Smartlead, Instantly, Expandi)
  • Hands-on n8n experience: building multi-step workflows with webhooks, API calls, branching logic, and error handling. Strong Make.com or Zapier builders who are ready to ramp on n8n quickly will be considered
  • Working knowledge of cold email deliverability
  • Experience with all major CRM platforms
  • Client-facing experience: you've run discovery calls, presented recommendations, and handled pushback
  • Strong writing skills. You'll write outreach copy, client-facing documents, and build notes. Copywriting can start with AI, but this role requires someone who knows how to turn an AI draft into a high-converting outreach message.
  • Sound judgment on outreach compliance (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, opt-out handling)

Nice to Have

  • Direct LGM experience
  • An agency or consulting background
  • Experience running outbound into PE-backed or mid-market companies
  • JavaScript or Python, for n8n Code nodes and custom data transformations
  • Familiarity with data providers such as Apollo, ZoomInfo, or Clearbit

What We Offer

  • Direct access to leadership and real influence over how the practice grows
  • A wide variety of client problems, so the work doesn't get repetitive

How to Apply

Send your resume and a video (5 minutes max) walking through a Clay table, n8n workflow, or outbound system you built. Cover the problem, how you built it, and what it produced. We won't review applications without a walkthrough.

Our mission is to make money work for everyone. And while having a great app is part of that, we pride ourselves on providing world-class support. By solving customers' problems, treating them fairly and being transparent, we believe we can make banking better 💪

Our Complaints team works alongside Customer Operations to make sure customers receive the best possible service, even when things go wrong. We put empathy at the heart of how we handle complaints and use what we learn to make things better.

As our Complaints Policy Manager, you'll lead a team of technical experts and shape how we handle complaints across Monzo. You'll bring together regulatory requirements, customer needs and operational priorities to make sure our policies are clear, effective and fair. You'll play an important role in strengthening our complaints framework, influencing decisions across the business and helping us deliver better customer outcomes at scale.

  • Partnering with Product, Legal, Risk, Compliance and Operations leaders to develop and embed policies, frameworks and operational changes that improve customer experiences.

  • You can build strong relationships across different teams, influence senior stakeholders and turn complex regulatory information into clear, practical guidance.

title: Engineering Manager, Enterprise Data Warehouse & Analytics
excerpt: Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country.
description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

Machinify brings together several payment integrity and recovery businesses for health plans. Each one produces numbers that executives, operations leaders, and clients act on. Your job is to make sure there is one warehouse, one conformed model, and one definition of every number.

The foundation is already in production: a Databricks lakehouse with 600+ dbt models, 1,800+ automated tests, Power BI semantic models, and LLM self-service on governed metrics. Your first priority isoperational measurement: building the trusted metrics our Operations leaders run their business on. Next, you'll extend the warehouse to new business domains with a repeatable, template-driven approach.

This is a hands-on Engineering Manager role on a flat team. You'll manage engineers and analysts directly and spend about half your time building: designing the dimensional model, writing and reviewing code, and setting the engineering standards. You'll partner closely with a Product counterpart who owns priorities and stakeholder intake, so you can focus on architecture, delivery, and the team.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the data model. Design and evolve the conformed dimensional model and the standards the team builds against. Review every new model for grain and conformance.
  • Build and run the pipelines. Design ETL/ELT from source systems through bronze → silver → gold on Databricks, with incremental loads, data contracts, and Airflow orchestration.
  • Own the semantic layer. Build governed metrics in Unity Catalog metric views and Power BI semantic models, so every dashboard, report, and LLM query uses the same definitions.
  • Deliver reliable operational metrics. Turn KPI definitions from Product and Operations into certified models and metrics, reconciled to source and delivered through dashboards and self-service.
  • Assure the numbers. Own reconciliation, data tests, freshness and anomaly monitoring, SLOs, and CI/CD for data.
  • Modernize orchestration. Lead the move of dbt orchestration from dbt Cloud to Airflow without gaps in data freshness.
  • Partner with Product. Work with your Product counterpart and business stakeholders to shape requirements. You own the technical plan: architecture, sequencing, estimates, and trade-offs.
  • Lead the team. Manage, coach, and hire analytics engineers and BI analysts. Run sprint execution and set the bar for code review, testing, documentation, and AI-assisted development.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years in data warehousing, data engineering, or analytics engineering, including 3+ years as a hands-on engineering manager.
  • Expert in dimensional modeling: grain, fact types, conformed dimensions, slowly changing dimensions, bridge tables, and the bus matrix. Has built an enterprise warehouse across multiple source systems and owned it in production
  • Expert SQL and dbt: complex SQL and performance tuning; dbt models, tests, macros, packages, and CI
  • Databricks in production: Spark SQL, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and medallion architecture. Deep Snowflake or BigQuery experience will be considered
  • Semantic layer: has built governed metrics (Databricks metric views, dbt Semantic Layer/MetricFlow, Cube, or Power BI semantic models) and the BI on top. Power BI/DAX preferred
  • ETL/ELT and orchestration: has designed and run production pipelines with incremental loads, snapshots or CDC, and Airflow (or a similar orchestrator). Python for pipeline work
  • Data quality: testing, reconciliation, observability, and CI/CD for data
  • Cross-functional partner: works well with a Product counterpart and business stakeholders. Turns requirements into technical designs and explains trade-offs in plain language

Nice to have

  • Healthcare claims or payment integrity data
  • Building operational KPIs with business operators
  • LLM-based self-service analytics (e.g., Databricks Genie)
  • Experience leading teams across time zones

What We Offer

  • Work from anywhere in the US! Machinify is digital-first.
  • Full Medical/Dental/Vision for employees & their families
  • Flexible and trusting environment where you’ll feel empowered to do your best work
  • Unlimited FTO
  • Competitive salary, equity, 401(k) including employer match

Base Salary: $220,000-$260,000

The salary for this position is based on an array of factors unique to each candidate: Such as years and depth of experience, set skills, certifications, etc. We are hiring for different levels, and our Recruiting team will let you know if you qualify for a different role/range. Salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes meaningful equity, excellent healthcare, flexible time off, and other benefits and perks.

description:

Location: Remote:

About FamilyWell Health

FamilyWell Health is a Series A women's behavioral health company embedding the Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) into OB/GYN, primary care, and adjacent women's health practices. Our model enables women’s health providers to deliver equitable, affordable, evidence-based mental health care to their patients while generating sustainable revenue for their practices through CoCM billing, including Medicare and Medicaid populations. FamilyWell is one of the fastest-growing companies in women's behavioral health, currently serving patients across six states with continued national expansion underway. To learn more about FamilyWell, please visit.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Reproductive Psychiatrist who is passionate about our mission, loves to mentor and train clinicians, and build high-functioning teams. This is a unique opportunity to oversee clinical excellence at FamilyWell and shape the future of integrated women's mental health care. The medical director will play a pivotal role in developing evidence-based treatment protocols, overseeing clinical quality, and ensuring exceptional patient outcomes across the reproductive mental health spectrum. The Medical Director will initially report directly to the CEO and serve as a key clinical voice in strategic planning, product design, and patient experience. This position is virtual with flexible work hours.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Leadership

  • Provide clinical oversight and supervision for provider teams including psychiatric nurse practitioners and therapists.
  • Develop and implement evidence-based treatment protocols evaluating impact on patient outcomes and revenue sustainability
  • Build and oversee quality assurance to ensure adherence to clinical best practices, safety standards, and regulatory compliance.
  • Provide clinical supervision and mentorship for psychiatric nurse practitioners, conducting case reviews and supporting direct patient care.
  • Lead the clinical strategy and vision for women's reproductive mental health services.
  • Partner closely with executive leadership to shape the strategic direction of FamilyWell by providing clinical expertise that drives the development and expansion of innovative service offerings and clinical programs.
  • Analyze data and clinical outcomes to develop insights for clinical practice and presentation of thought leadership both internally and externally.
  • Stay current with emerging research and integrate new findings into clinical practice.
  • Participate in product development and clinical innovation initiatives.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Establish and maintain clinical quality metrics and outcome measures.
  • Ensure compliance with state licensing requirements, HIPAA, and other regulatory standards.
  • Oversee risk management protocols and patient safety initiatives.
  • Develop and maintain clinical documentation standards.

Team Leadership

Clinical Leader

Mission Driven

Culture of Clinical Excellence & Continuous Improvement

Key Competencies We Will Assess

Clinical Expertise in Reproductive Psychiatry

  • Evaluated through clinical case review during the interview process.

Adaptability & Agility

  • Ability to pivot quickly and thrive without a lot of structure.
  • Demonstrated strength and comfort navigating ambiguity while contributing to cross-functional initiatives beyond direct clinical care.
  • Previous experience serving as a Medical Director or other clinical leadership role at a mental health or digital health startup is strongly preferred.

Leadership, Team Building & Mentorship

Comprehensive Benefits Package

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Retirement plan
  • Professional development and continuing education support
  • PTO & holiday coverage
  • Family leave benefit

Professional Growth

  • Leadership role in scaling women's mental health services
  • Access to cutting-edge AI technologies
  • Collaboration with a multidisciplinary team of experts
  • Speaking and publication opportunities

Work-Life Integration

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Physical IC Layout Engineer to join our growing US-based High-Performance Computing & Edge AI Power team.

You will contribute to next-generation power management solutions for AI data centers, high-performance computing, and advanced power delivery applications.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and implement full-chip and block-level physical layouts for analog, mixed-signal, and power management ICs (PMICs).

  • Collaborate closely with analog and digital design engineers to ensure layout quality and design integrity.
  • Serve as the primary technical liaison between US and China engineering teams, facilitating design reviews and technical discussions in English and Mandarin.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on IC layout experience in analog, mixed-signal, or power management IC design.

  • Fluent in English and Mandarin Chinese (Required), with strong technical communication skills.
  • Proficiency in Cadence Virtuoso and Calibre or equivalent DRC/LVS/ERC verification tools.
  • Strong understanding of device matching, guard rings, deep N-well, ESD/latch-up, electromigration, and layout-dependent effects.
  • Ability to collaborate across global engineering teams and independently manage technical challenges.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with 130nm or 180nm process technologies.
  • Familiarity with DC-DC converters, switching regulators, multiphase controllers, or power management IC architectures.
  • Previous experience coordinating layout development across geographically distributed teams.

Customer Experience Associate

Peerspace · Customer Experience · Entry level

Peerspace is the leading and category defining online marketplace for venue rentals for meetings, productions, and events. We open doors to the most inspiring spaces around the world, from lofts and mansions to storefronts and studios. Over $500M has been transacted through the platform, and our investors include GV (Google Ventures) and Foundation Capital.

Our people are the heart of Peerspace. We are a team that values inclusion and working cross functionally. Our strategy and objectives are clear and we support one another to exceed expectations. We believe that a healthy company culture creates an environment where people are excited to come into work everyday and contribute to building a successful organization.

About the role

Most routine questions get answered before they ever reach a person. What's left are the conversations that actually need one: a host and a guest who remember the same booking differently, a photographer whose shoot starts in three hours and the space just fell through, a situation where we don’t have a policy in place to resolve.

That's the work. As a Customer Experience Associate, you'll handle the cases that require judgment, empathy, and a bit of creative problem solving; and in the process you'll learn how a two-sided marketplace actually works, from the inside out.

What you'll do

  • Work a queue of guest and host conversations across chat, email, phone, and SMS, focused on the cases that were routed to a person for a reason.

  • Resolve booking issues, mediate misunderstandings between hosts and guests, and process cancellations and adjustments accurately.

  • Use our AI assist tools and knowledge base to draft and check responses; then edit for accuracy and tone. You're the one who decides what actually gets sent.

  • Look for chances to surprise and delight someone, and take them.

  • Flag recurring issues, confusing policies, and product friction to Specialists and leadership so they get fixed rather than re-answered.

  • Hit response-time and quality targets while keeping careful, complete case notes.

  • Show up for your team: standups, Slack etc… be a part of the culture that makes this a stellar place to work.

What we're looking for

You lead with empathy and keep the customer's interest front and center, even when the answer is no. You write clearly and warmly, and you care about grammar and tone. You can carry a case all the way to resolution without being chased, and you know the difference between a call you should make yourself and one you should escalate.

You're comfortable with technology and genuinely curious about working alongside AI tools. You are confident enough to use them well, but skeptical enough to check their work. New tools and policy changes don't rattle you. You can read your own queue and quality metrics and do something useful with what they tell you.

On paper, that usually looks like:

  • 1–2 years experience in customer service, hospitality, support, or something adjacent.

  • Strong writing skills with real attention to detail.

  • A sense of humor and genuine enthusiasm for helping people.

  • Bonus points if you have third party marketplace experience.

  • Additional bonus points for any experience with Intercom.

Schedule - 4 week rotation:

  • Weeks 1-3:

    • Monday - Friday; 8 hours/day (hours flexible depending on time zone)

  • Week 4:

    • Monday & Tuesday; 8 hours/day (hours flexible depending on time zone)

    • Wednesday & Thursday; OFF

    • Friday - Sunday; 8 hours/day (hours flexible depending on time zone)

The hourly rate for this role is $25.00/hour.

About Figure

Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Portfolio & Investment Operations Manager to join our growing team! As Portfolio & Investment Operations Manager, you’ll own asset management for a portfolio of residential transition loans (RTL)/bridge loans and home equity lines of credit (HELOCs) across securitizations, forward flow agreements, and joint ventures. You’ll be the primary point of accountability for the ongoing performance, compliance, and economics of these portfolios and joint ventures, bridging deal structuring and live operations by turning portfolio management objectives and servicing, warehouse, and sale documents into repeatable practices. This is a newly created role on our Capital Markets team, supporting a leading structured finance platform with multiple institutional counterparties.

What You’ll Do

  • Track performance of mortgage assets, including origination trends, payoffs, delinquency, extensions, draws, and loss metrics across warehouse and owned positions
  • Produce recurring portfolio reports for internal and institutional stakeholders, and support board and investor reporting cycles
  • Maintain a current view of concentration limits, eligibility criteria, and covenant compliance across the portfolio
  • Build and maintain portfolio dashboards and trackers covering performance, cash flows, and key risk metrics
  • Manage day-to-day portfolio operations, including delinquency tracking and cash and collateral reconciliation
  • Apply the portfolio’s governing agreements to day-to-day decisions, including expense sharing, decision rights, and waterfall mechanics
  • Support forward flow and loan sale relationships, including compliance with applicable purchase and forward flow agreements
  • Coordinate with Legal and Compliance on counterparty notifications, consents, and amendments as the portfolio evolves
  • Oversee investment vehicle mechanics for joint ventures, including capital calls, distributions, and investor reporting cycles
  • Partner with deal and transaction management, structuring, and compliance teams on new originations, securitizations, and portfolio sales
  • Work with Finance and Accounting on cash reconciliation, fee distributions, and portfolio economics

What We Look For

  • 4+ years in portfolio or asset management, structured finance, or capital markets operations, with direct exposure to residential transition loans, HELOCs, RMBS, or warehouse-financed loan portfolios
  • Comfort interpreting and applying governing agreements, servicing agreements, and financing documents
  • Ability to read and apply legal and transaction documents directly rather than relying on summaries
  • Strong Excel, SQL, Python, Tableau, and financial modeling skills, with comfort building and maintaining portfolio tracking and reporting tools

  • Experience with fund or investment vehicle administration, including capital calls, distributions, and investor reporting cycles (preferred)

Location: Remote, New York City, or Oakland, CA

Role Type: Full-time

Compensation: $135,000 or $155,000, depending on seniority

Reports to: Chief Administrative Officer

Visa sponsorship: Not available

Hires remotely in: United States

-

About the Role

The Operational Excellence Lead will connect the organization's long-horizon, cross-functional, and external-facing strategy with internal execution. They will build the operating cadence, information flow, and forums that let the organization run performance-versus-plan at every level, and own the follow-through that keeps decisions and strategy connected across altitudes.

What Success Looks Like

  • Leaders know where and why core impact metrics are moving, and how to intervene.
  • Forums at every altitude (team level, functional leads, leads review) run with clear owners, decisions, and metrics.
  • Operational systems drive high-quality, consistent reporting and better decision-making.
  • Resourcing decisions are data-driven, and ROI is tracked over time.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Strategy & Operating Cadence

Own the connective layer between long-term vision and strategy, and functional leads' near-term execution.

  • Run performance-versus-plan and OKR processes across the organization, working with leads to define outcomes, metrics, and reporting cadence. Own core planning cycles (e.g., H2 planning) end to end — the calendar, the templates, and the cross-team dependencies.
  • Consolidate fragmented ownership, and make ownership, decision-making, and escalation paths explicit.
  • Facilitate cross-functional reviews that ladder up into organizational strategy; ask sharp questions, capture action items with clear owners and dates, and enforce time-boxing so discussions actually converge.
  • Communicate internally about our impact metric progress by owning the Impact Monthly meeting: build the update deck, and work with teams across the org to source the case studies and highlights that make it concrete.
  • Partner with the Director of Talent to create org-wide communications calendar and content based on critical happenings.

Data & Financial Analysis

Ensures the organization has trustworthy, accessible data to run performance-versus-plan, understand unit economics and make resourcing decisions.

  • Support the business case for strategic initiatives such as headcount requests, RFPs, or resourcing requests — making the value proposition clear and concrete using business cases, OKRs, or other appropriate value frameworks — before they're resourced.
  • Pull and build your own analyses (e.g., in Looker) to diagnose what's driving or blocking core metrics like transitions, usage, CSAT, and launch momentum.
  • Use data and diagnosis, not authority, to earn the trust of a highly analytical engineering and impact organization.

Continuous Improvement

Drive better decision making, organizational design and operating orientation using data-driven insights

  • Pair alongside individual leaders on specific strategic challenges, both to bolster their output and to diagnose whether a gap is about skills, structure, or hiring.
  • Inform performance management and promotions with impact data.
  • Maintain a clear view of the organization's critical-path portfolio, including how it breaks down between funded work (what states or customers are paying us for) and unfunded work — a key input into planning and resourcing decisions.
  • Continuously improve the operational excellence function's own methodology — refining the templates, tools, and processes it runs on (e.g., the PVP sheet, planning docs, review formats) — and share what's working across teams rather than reinventing it in each forum.

Systems Management

Designs systems to capture and improve our unit economics

  • Help define requirements for and implement a revenue operationssystem.
  • Help the organization answer emerging questions about AI and tooling ROI.
  • Define clear requirements for measuring cloud costs or personnel costs by state, partnering with an internal engineer or data partner to build the dashboard once the requirements are clear — bringing the finance and business framing that a purely technical build can miss.

Who You'll Work With

You’ll report to the Chief Administrative Officer. Your initial focus is the Impact organization and the Engineering leadership team, together the “core impact apparatus.” You’ll work closely with functional and technical leads across Impact and Engineering and with data and systems teams. Over time, as the role’s scope expands, you’ll also work with leaders in marketing, business development, finance, and people operations.

What We're Looking For

  • A senior operator — likely from a product management, product operations or program management background.
  • Strong analytical skills and genuine comfort with data: able to pull your own analysis from tools like Looker and build a credible, data-driven case, even without a formal technical or engineering background.
  • High emotional intelligence: able to work with senior, strong-willed leaders and get them to take ownership, without dictating to them.
  • Excellent synthesis and written communication: able to hold many concurrent threads, re-articulate strategy clearly, and drive high-quality, fast follow-up.
  • A bias toward clarity and simplification — comfortable pushing to reduce the number of people involved in a decision or a meeting, not just adding structure.
  • Comfortable constructively challenging partners and leaders — willing to stress-test thinking and push back, not just surface issues and let them sit.
  • Steady under pressure; this role sits amid a lot of interpersonal complexity and needs someone with strong composure.
  • Comfortable operating with significant seniority and scope from day one — this is intended as a senior hire, not an entry point into strategy work.
  • Experience in government, public-sector, or B2G contexts, or with mission-driven and nonprofit organizations.
  • Experience running OKR or performance-versus-plan processes at scale.

Every decision our TPA business makes starts with financials people can trust, and you’re the one who makes that possible. As TPA Accounting Manager, you run the month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close for the TPA entity, making sure the books are accurate, compliant, and tightly controlled. excerpt: Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success.
description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We're looking for a Senior Director to own cross-functional prioritization and delivery across Mission Lane, reporting to the SVP, Product, Platform, & Delivery

The impact you'll make:

Every initiative Mission Lane ships – a better payment plan, a faster credit decision, a clearer way to see progress -- moves a customer forward. None of it ships in a vacuum. It depends on the right team picking it up at the right time, with the capacity to see it through, without adversely affecting another initiative.

The system that sorts through those prioritization decisions is yours to run. You’ll manage the framework and facilitate the discussions that decide what goes first when domains are moving at different speeds and carrying different risks. You'll often be bringing a room full of different perspectives to a shared answer.

This function is new at Mission Lane, and the framework for it is only partly in place. You're the one who fills in what's missing and runs it day to day, building the credibility that earns trust and adherence.

What you'll own:

  • A team of four Delivery Managers, each embedded in a different focus area (Collections, Data & AI/Model Process, Portfolio Management, and Acquisitions), including their coaching, growth, and workload balance
  • The prioritization tracker as Mission Lane's single source of truth for what's in flight, at what stage, and why, kept accurate enough that leaders trust it without double-checking
  • Weekly prioritization meetings, MBRs, and QBRs, run with enough rigor to hold up under executive scrutiny
  • Company-wide delivery standards, frameworks, and tooling that initiative teams actually adopt in their day-to-day work
  • Cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Credit, Marketing, Finance, and Legal/Compliance, clearing blockers and resolving trade-offs before they stall delivery
  • Post-initiative retrospectives that produce concrete changes to how the next initiative gets planned and delivered

You'll thrive in this role if:

  • You've led delivery inside an organization with genuine cross-functional complexity, spanning multiple teams and stakeholder groups.
  • You've built a prioritization or delivery process yourself, and can explain the tradeoffs in it clearly enough that someone new to it can follow the logic.
  • Your background is in product, program, or technical delivery leadership, with the credibility to work as a peer with engineering leads and data scientists.
  • You build just enough process to protect capacity and speed, no more.
  • You have direct conversations with senior stakeholders when priorities conflict, and you know how to bring a room to a decision.

Minimum qualifications:

  • A proven track record of building processes and oversight to drive improved speed to impact across an organization.
  • A proven track record leading and developing a team focused on organizational effectiveness which could include Delivery Managers, Program Managers, or similarly scoped delivery leaders
  • Experience working in a highly regulated and technical environment, with demonstrated ability to shape functional strategy and operate with a high degree of autonomy
  • Experience owning enterprise-level portfolio intake, prioritization, and execution tracking end to end, at a company operating at meaningful scale and complexity
  • A demonstrated ability to align senior and executive stakeholders across functions such as Product, Engineering, Finance, Credit, and Legal around shared priorities without relying on direct authority
  • Deep working knowledge of modern delivery methodologies and the judgment to adapt them to an organization's actual stage of maturity as well as rapidly changing technology
  • Experience structuring and running core enterprise operating cadences, such as weekly prioritization meetings, MBRs, and QBRs, that senior leadership relies on for accurate decision-making
  • Hands-on experience with modern portfolio and workflow tooling (e.g., Jira, Jira Align, Asana, Monday.com, Smartsheet), including evaluating and administering these tools at an organizational level
  • A background that includes hiring, coaching, and developing direct reports
  • Ability to travel ~4+ times per year for high quality in person collaboration

Preferred qualifications:

  • Direct experience in consumer lending, credit cards, or another regulated financial services environment, with working knowledge of compliance, credit risk, and legal considerations that shape delivery timelines
  • Experience scaling delivery governance and team structures inside a fast-growing, mid-sized organization moving through a similar stage of process maturity
  • Expertise configuring enterprise-grade portfolio tools (e.g., Jira Align, Dragonboat, Productboard) to connect strategic goals directly to team execution

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

  • Complete Sprout Social’s new hire training & onboarding program alongside other new Sprout team members. You’ll gain a broader understanding of our products and how your role fits into the organization.

  • Shadow the current close cycle, ELT/Board reporting process, and key corporate dashboards to understand how they come together today.

Within 3 months, you’ll start hitting your stride by:

  • Contributing directly to ELT, Board, and IR reporting materials with increasing autonomy.

Within 6 months, you’ll be making a clear impact through:

  • Owning key corporate reports and dashboards in Pigment end-to-end, with minimal oversight.
  • Proactively flagging data or process issues before they become reporting risks.
  • Taking on ad hoc modeling requests with sound judgment on approach and prioritization.

Within 12 months, you’ll make this role your own by:

  • Operating as a trusted, go-to analytical partner within the Corporate FP&A team.
  • Driving improvements to existing reporting processes and dashboards in Pigment, reducing manual effort where possible.
  • Taking on a broader scope of corporate reporting and modeling responsibilities as the team and business scale.

Of course, what is outlined above is the ideal timeline, but things may shift based on business needs and other projects and tasks could be added at the discretion of your manager.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Overview

The Customer Experience (CX) team sits at the center of Instacart’s support ecosystem, serving our diverse community of consumers, shoppers, retailers, and advertisers through both direct support and scalable solutions. We partner closely with cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, and Operations to surface insights from the front line, reduce friction in the customer journey, and shape future roadmaps.

We deliver empathetic, high-quality support through a blend of data-driven, operational excellence. By focusing on clear communication, critical thinking, and continuous improvement, we ensure that every customer interaction not only resolves the immediate issue but also consistently enhances the overall Instacart experience.

About the Job

  • This role plays a vital part in supporting our consumers, shoppers, retailers, and advertisers. We are currently hiring for a variety of shifts, including morning, mid-day, and evening coverage, to ensure we provide seamless service throughout the day. Schedule flexibility—including availability for evenings, weekends, and holidays—is essential to meeting the diverse needs of our community.
  • Handle live customer contacts (phone, chat, and/or email) for up to 100% of your scheduled time, consistently delivering clear, empathetic, and efficient support.

About You

Minimum qualifications

  • Fluency in French, both spoken and written
  • Comfort handling live contacts for most of the day (phone, chat, and/or email) in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment

  • Problem-solving mindset with the ability to investigate issues, interpret account/order details, and make sound judgments within policy

  • Schedule flexibility to support evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs

Work Schedule

excerpt: Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company.
description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

We are recruiting US-based architects and certified plans examiners to evaluate the output of an AI system that performs automated building-code compliance review on architectural permit applications.

The system ingests permit submissions — new builds, alterations, modifications — and issues a compliant or non-compliant determination for each applicable check, drawn from the International Building Code. Every determination comes with a cited code provision and a marked location on the drawing set showing the evidence relied upon.

Your job is to tell us where the system got it wrong. You are applying the same judgment you already apply in plan review or permit preparation, to a set of determinations that have already been made. Where the system is correct, you confirm it. Where it is wrong, you correct it and the correction becomes training signal.

This is expert review work, not data entry. There is no volume of repetitive clicking to grind through and no generalist labeling pool to compete with — the entire premise of the program is that these judgments cannot be made by anyone without real code expertise.

What You’ll Own:

  • Review and correct pass/fail verdicts, written rationales, and citation boxes on PDF plans using the in-tool editing toolkit.
  • QA and correct labeling: Review AI-generated outputs, fix mislabeled data, and grade agent performance against what a real permit reviewer would conclude.
  • Interpret permitting checklists as an experienced reviewer would, applying the relevant requirements to the submitted plans.
  • Trace checklist requirements to their applicable source: IBC, IRC or other model codes, state building codes, or county/jurisdiction-specific amendments. Explain which requirement applies and why.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

  • ICC certification relevant to building plan review, plus actual experience reviewing permit applications and issuing or resolving plan review comments.
  • Based in the United States, with at least 2 years of hands-on permitting experience; 5+ years strongly preferred.
  • Deep knowledge of how permitting actually works in the United States, with a preference for experience in Arizona, California, Florida, or Texas.
  • Plan examiner or Certified Building Official (CBO) experience and credentials. Provide certification details and the jurisdictions and project types you have reviewed.

The expected hourly range for this position is $50-$75 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

title: Technical Product Owner – Salesforce Health Cloud & AI-Enabled Agile Delivery
excerpt: We are looking for a Product Owner who wants to shape a product, not administer a backlog.
description:
We are looking for a Product Owner who wants to shape a product, not administer a backlog. In this role you will own what our development team builds and why, for the Salesforce Health Cloud solutions that power a fast-growing patient services business. You will help shape the roadmap alongside our Innovation and Implementation leaders, then carry it all the way through to working software that clients and patient-facing teams actually use.

This is a decision-making seat on a small, fast-moving team. There is no room for ambiguity: you set priority, you resolve the open questions blocking a build, and you say no when something does not fit. You will also work as part of a broader technology organization, partnering with our AI Lead, data team, and IT operations group to make sure solutions fit the platform rather than bolt onto it.

We expect you to work with AI, not around it. The team runs on Jira, Confluence, and Rovo and uses Claude, Claude Code, and Agentforce Vibes in its daily practice. Used well, these tools take the drafting burden out of stories, specifications, and test scenarios so your time goes where it matters most: discovery with the business, hard prioritization calls, and validating that what we built solves the actual problem.

Success in this role is shared. You will own product outcomes - what shipped and whether it works - and share accountability with the Innovation and Impact team for what happens after go-live: adoption, efficiency gains, and measurable return. The Delivery Manager owns delivery flow and predictability. All of it in service of our mission to remove barriers between patients and the care they need.

Core Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Roadmap Partnership: Contribute to the product roadmap with the Executive Director of IT Development, Innovation and Impact, and Implementation leaders - bringing the platform view, feasibility, and sequencing realities into strategy conversations before commitments are made.
  • Value-Driven Prioritization: Own a single prioritized backlog spanning client launches, enhancements, defects, and platform work. Make the trade-offs explicit, publish the rationale, and keep the backlog an honest reflection of what the team will actually do.
  • Specification & Story Decomposition: Translate complex business needs into build-ready, incrementally deliverable work for Salesforce Health Cloud. Decompose capabilities and workflows into epics, features/user stories, and acceptance criteria at the right level for engineering execution. Define the required data model, business and validation rules, automations, role-based access, integrations, notifications, dependencies, and exception scenarios. Identify gaps and decisions before development begins and confirm the resulting solution against what the business meant, not only what was initially asked for.
  • Backlog Readiness: Own the readiness of work before sprint commitment. Ensure stories have sufficient requirements, acceptance criteria, dependencies, design decisions, data and access needs, and test scenarios for engineering to begin without avoidable discovery or requirements churn during the sprint. Ensure decisions and requirement changes are reflected in the backlog as the source of truth.
  • AI-Enhanced Workflows: Use Claude, Claude Code, Agentforce Vibes, and Rovo to accelerate research, story writing, documentation, and test scenario generation - with the review discipline and data handling standards a regulated environment requires.
  • Stakeholder Synthesis: Act as the primary point of contact for Market Access, Clinical Adherence, Pharmacy, Revenue Cycle Management, Implementation, and Compliance stakeholders. Negotiate competing priorities and manage expectations without relying on positional authority.
  • Outcomes Over Output: Define the success measures for what you ship, then go look. Track adoption, error and rework rates, cycle time, and operational impact after release, and use what you learn to reshape the backlog.
  • Delivery Accountability: Partner daily with the Delivery Manager, who owns the delivery flow, sprint capacity, sequencing, and delivery predictability. The Product Owner owns priority, scope, requirements, and product decisions during the sprint. Define acceptance criteria, accept completed work, and make timely scope and priority decisions when tradeoffs are required.
  • Quality, Release & Business Readiness: Define how each requirement gets tested, lead user acceptance testing with the business, and triage defects through resolution. Demonstrate completed functionality to stakeholders, coordinate and deliver operational training, and confirm the business is prepared to adopt the change before go-live. Ensure documentation, training materials, communications, and post-deployment verification are complete before release.
  • Platform Stewardship: Work with the Salesforce architect on configuration-first, reusable solutions that limit technical debt; with the AI Lead on where automation and AI belong in patient services workflows, including the guardrails; and with the data team on reporting, analytics, and integration requirements.
  • Compliance by Design: Build HIPAA obligations, security policy, and minimum-necessary access into requirements from the start, given the patient, provider, and payer data our programs touch.

Skills & Requirements:

  • 3+ years as a Product Owner in an agile environment, with direct ownership of a backlog and the priority calls that come with it.
  • A track record of taking digital products from concept to launch and being able to say what changed as a result.
  • Working knowledge of the Salesforce platform and its configuration model - objects, fields, record types, permission sets, flows, and reporting. Health Cloud experience is a strong advantage.
  • The ability to write requirements a developer can build from and a tester can verify against independently.
  • Data literacy: comfort defining metrics, working with reports and dashboards, and using evidence rather than volume of requests to drive decisions.
  • Practical experience with generative AI tools for documentation, analysis, and agile workflows.
  • Exceptional communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence without authority and to hold a position under pressure.
  • Comfort operating at pace with incomplete information, in a fully remote environment where accountability is self-driven.

Education, Certifications and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Healthcare Administration, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience in patient services, patient access, hub services, specialty pharmacy, market access, or revenue cycle management a strong advantage.
  • Hands-on experience with Jira and Confluence preferred; familiarity with Atlassian Rovo, Claude, or comparable AI assistants preferred.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA and regulated healthcare environments preferred.
  • Relevant certifications preferred, including: Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), Professional Scrum Product Owner (PSPO), PMI-PBA, Salesforce Certified Administrator, Salesforce Certified Business Analyst, or Salesforce Health Cloud Accredited Professional.

Physical Requirements:

  • As a remote-forward organization, this position operates in a virtual professional office environment and teleworking from the employee’s home address listed in their employment file.
  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Keyboarding
  • Speaking
  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times
  • Flexibility of working hours to support activities across EST to PST zones
  • Minimal travel possible

Our PRO-Spectus Culture Philosophy

At PRO-Spectus we have created a culture that is supportive, dedicated, and teamwork driven. We celebrate each other’s joys in personal life and professional accomplishments, promoting meaningful relationships and friendships.

Our employees bring strength of mind and spirit to make the extraordinary happen every day. With humility and compassion at our core, PRO-Spectus is proud of our relentless focus towards the higher purpose of improving the lives of patients we support.

We recognize it takes a lot of people working together with a common goal to make spectacular happen, and we never forget that at the heart of our company are the people who make it work.

PRO-Spectus is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer. All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, protected veteran status, marital status or other protected status under federal, state or local laws.

At PRO-spectus, we are deeply committed to pay transparency and equity. The annual range for this position is $115,000 - 140,000, based on experience and qualifications, with the final offer reflecting skills and other job-related factors. Beyond competitive pay, we offer a comprehensive and generous benefits package designed to support your well-being and work-life balance.

Our benefits include robust medical, dental, and vision plans; life insurance and disability coverage; and tax-advantaged savings accounts. We also provide an Employee Assistance Program, home office benefits, and unique perks like an Employee Ownership Program. With paid time off, holidays, bereavement leave, and a 401(k)-retirement plan with employer matching, PRO-spectus prioritizes your financial and personal security. Plus, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus opportunity.

Join PRO-spectus, where your career growth, well-being, and contributions truly matter!
