excerpt: Content Editor (Contract, Project Basis) About Arora Media Arora Media is an award-winning growth consulting firm founded 6 years ago.
description:
Content Editor (Contract, Project Basis)

About Arora Media

Arora Media is an award-winning growth consulting firm founded 6 years ago. We work with leading CPG, SaaS, DTC, and commerce brands, and we run everything through three divisions: Performance, Operations, and Activations. Performance grows the company through paid and organic. Operations builds the internal systems to handle that scale. Activations connects brands with their customers beyond the screen: events, pop-ups, student ambassadors, and more.

We are not like other companies you have worked for. We are built on culture, giving 110% to everything we do in and outside of the workplace. We like to promote within, build skills from the ground up, and keep moving forward regardless of our circumstances. We believe in hiring people, not skills.

The Role

We need a content editor who can take a long conversation and turn it into a short video that actually holds attention. Think a16z on Instagram: clean cuts, real storytelling, captions that carry the point, pacing that makes a 60 second clip feel like it earned your time.

This is contract work, paid per project. When we have a video, we reach out, you cut it, and you get paid for that project. No retainer, no set hours. Around 5 videos a month, around 4 days turnaround per video.

What You Will Do

  • Turn long-form conversations into short-form Instagram videos that tell a story, not just a highlight reel
  • Own the narrative: pick the hook, structure the arc, storyboard the flow before you cut
  • Use AI tools as part of your editing process, not as a replacement for taste
  • Bring your own creative ideas to every cut, not just execute a brief
  • Deliver polished, professional edits that match the Arora Media standard

What You Will Bring

  • A portfolio of edited short-form video, ideally interview or conversation driven, story first
  • A strong sense of pacing, story structure, and what makes someone stop scrolling
  • Real experience with AI editing tools and a workflow for using them
  • Storyboarding skills, you can show the plan before the edit
  • Professional, reliable, and fast without cutting corners

- Based in the United States preferred

The Details

- Contract, paid per project

- Around 5 videos a month

- Around 4 days turnaround per video

  • We reach out when a video is ready to cut

How to Apply

Apply on this listing, and send your portfolio to as well. Both steps. If we like your work, we will reach out with a test project.

EEO and Accommodations

Arora Media is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to attracting, developing and retaining highly qualified talent who empower our innovative teams through unique perspectives and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans' status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Arora Media will also consider qualified applications with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Arora Media welcomes and encourages applications from individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates during all aspects of the selection process. Please advise the talent acquisition team or contact if you require accommodations during the interview process.

excerpt: LTK’s mission is to empower the world’s premium lifestyle Creators to achieve maximum economic success.
description:
LTK’s mission is to empower the world’s premium lifestyle Creators to achieve maximum economic success. We have a huge opportunity ahead of us and we’re looking for team members who want to create, innovate and disrupt an industry.

We empower our team members to drive innovation, create value, and continue to spearhead the creation of this industry — a game changer when it comes to career growth.

Position title: Client Partner, Strategic New Business

Location: Remote, with a strong preference for candidates in the New York City area
Travel: Regular travel and weekly in-person client engagement expected

About the role

LTK is looking for a Client Partner, Strategic New Business to drive enterprise growth by bringing high-potential brands into the LTK ecosystem. This is a true hunter role for someone who thrives on opening doors, creating demand, building executive relationships, and turning opportunities into meaningful new partnerships.

You'll own the full new-business sales cycle, from identifying priority brands and uncovering their business challenges to developing compelling pitches, negotiating, and securing initial investment. Using LTK's proprietary creator-commerce data, AI-powered technology, and suite of solutions, you'll help brands see new possibilities for connecting creators, consumers, and commerce to measurable business outcomes.

The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, commercially driven, and a compelling storyteller who knows how to turn insights into action. You'll spend meaningful time in market, building relationships with senior brand and agency leaders, and positioning LTK as a strategic partner in the evolving creator-commerce landscape.

How you will make an impact

Win New Business

  • Own a portfolio of priority target brands, developing acquisition strategies to win new enterprise partnerships.
  • Generate qualified pipeline through proactive prospecting, strategic outreach, relationship development, and market intelligence.
  • Identify and build relationships with key decision-makers, champions, and budget owners within target organizations.
  • Lead opportunities through the full sales cycle, from initial engagement and discovery through negotiation and close.
  • Maintain a disciplined pipeline, accurate revenue forecasts, and clear strategies to accelerate conversion.
  • Spend meaningful time in market through weekly in-person prospect meetings, executive presentations, and industry events.
  • Partner with internal teams to align on commercial commitments, support initial brand activation, and ensure a smooth transition to ongoing account management.

Build the Case for LTK

  • Lead consultative discovery to uncover brand objectives, marketing challenges, and opportunities for growth.
  • Identify the right entry point across LTK's solutions, including Managed Services, Quick Collabs, and Gifting, based on each prospect's needs.
  • Partner with Strategy and Analytics to translate LTK's proprietary creator-commerce data and AI-powered insights into compelling commercial opportunities.
  • Develop tailored pitches and proposals that connect brand challenges to clear investment recommendations and measurable outcomes.
  • Present recommendations to senior brand, marketing, and agency decision-makers, positioning LTK as a strategic partner rather than a transactional solution.
  • Collaborate with Product, Brand Success, Legal, Finance, and Operations to develop solutions that are commercially compelling and executable.
  • Bring prospect feedback, competitive intelligence, and emerging market opportunities back to LTK to strengthen positioning and inform future growth opportunities.

What you will bring to LTK

  • 5+ years of experience in enterprise sales, business development, strategic partnerships, or a related commercial role.
  • Demonstrated track record of winning net-new enterprise business, consistently achieving revenue targets, and managing an individual sales quota.
  • Strong prospecting and business development capabilities, including identifying opportunities, opening doors, and building relationships with senior decision-makers.
  • Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from discovery through negotiation and close.
  • Strong consultative selling skills, with the ability to diagnose business challenges and develop tailored commercial solutions.
  • Strong analytical and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate data and business insights into persuasive executive-level pitches and investment recommendations.
  • Executive presence, commercial judgment, and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence senior decision-makers.
  • Proven ability to build and manage qualified pipeline, forecast revenue, and prioritize high-value opportunities.
  • An entrepreneurial, resourceful, and persistent approach to winning new business.
  • Willingness to travel regularly and prioritize weekly in-person prospect engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in creator marketing, influencer marketing, social commerce, affiliate marketing, or performance marketing.
  • Experience selling media, SaaS, ad tech, martech, platform, or managed-service solutions to enterprise brands.
  • Established relationships with senior brand, marketing, or agency decision-makers.
  • Familiarity with using commerce data, consumer insights, or AI-powered technology to inform sales strategies and client recommendations.

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistently achieve or exceed revenue targets through increased investment across existing enterprise partnerships.
  • Build measurable account-growth plans and qualified expansion pipelines across priority accounts.
  • Expand relationships across senior stakeholders, business units, and budget owners.
  • Increase share of wallet and adoption of LTK's platform solutions based on demonstrated client needs.
  • Retain and strengthen strategic partnerships by proactively addressing revenue risks and delivering measurable client value.

What we offer for full-time salaried employees

  • The opportunity to be part of the leading global company in creator commerce
  • A remote-first, productivity-first environment
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package to meet the needs of you and your family
  • 401(k) with LTK company matching
  • Medical Insurance, Vision Insurance, Dental Insurance
  • Paid Maternity Leave and Paid Paternity Leave
  • Summer Fridays and Flexible PTO
  • For temporary full-time employees, benefits eligibility may vary

About LTK

Founded in 2011, LTK is the global technology platform purpose-built to empower lifestyle creators to monetize their content. The full-service platform connects brands, creators, and shoppers with a world-class shopping app and trusted tools and technology that make content instantly shoppable. Today, premium lifestyle creators in 160+ countries drive more than $5 billion+ in annual retail sales through their LTK Shop profiles. More than 40 million consumers turn to LTK Shops in the LTK shopping platform each month to find inspiration and instantly shop the styles recommended by their favorite creators. More than 8,000 retailers and 1M brands partner with LTK to gain access to its global creator network for content that converts against performance-driven, cross-channel KPIs. LTK is headquartered in Dallas, TX, and currently operates on five continents.

Our mission

To empower the world’s premium lifestyle Creators to achieve maximum economic success.

Our values

  • Here to win
  • Commit to the journey
  • Work well

Commitment to diversity

LTK believes diversity, equity, and inclusion are fundamental obligations that strengthen our team. We employ a diverse, multi-disciplinary team to build a meaningful company and culture.

For US-Based Roles: We are not offering new sponsorships opportunities at this time for persons requiring employment visas, such as an H-1B; authorization to work in the U.S. is a precondition of employment.

Any unsolicited resumes/candidate profiles submitted through our website or to personal email accounts of employees of LTK are considered the property of LTK and are not subject to payment of agency fees.

LTK is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Senior Payroll Accountant
excerpt: Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential.
description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We are looking for a Senior Payroll Accountant to own payroll accounting and close for Oura's Global Payroll function. You will make sure payroll is recorded accurately in the general ledger, payroll balances are reconciled and explainable, and close deliverables are on time and audit-ready. You will also bring senior payroll expertise to day-to-day execution and coverage across US and international payrolls.This role suits someone who understands both how payroll is calculated and how it lands in the books, and who wants to make that connection more automated as we move to Workday.

What You Will Do:

  • Own payroll accounting and close. Prepare payroll journal entries, accruals, reclasses and cost allocations across entities, and explain payroll expense and liability variances to Accounting and FP&A.
  • Reconcile payroll balances. Prepare monthly payroll tax, benefit and net pay liability reconciliations, and tie payroll registers to funding, bank activity and the general ledger.
  • Keep controls audit-ready. Execute payroll accounting controls, maintain complete evidence, and prepare support for SOX testing and external audit.
  • Validate and automate. Test Workday payroll accounting outputs and GL integration, and automate manual reconciliations and variance checks.
  • Partner with the team on payroll execution. Support regular and off-cycle payroll processing, resolve discrepancies, support tax payments, and work with the Equity team on tax withholding and reconciliation for equity events.
  • Mentor. Serve as the team's payroll accounting resource and coach payroll administrators.

This is a remote role based in the US.

What you'll bring

  • 7+ years in payroll accounting, payroll or accounting operations, with hands-on ownership of payroll journal entries and reconciliations.
  • Strong accounting foundation: accruals, reconciliations, variance analysis, payroll liabilities and month-end close.
  • Working knowledge of payroll processing, payroll taxes, benefits and deductions, and year-end.
  • Experience with a major payroll or HCM system; Workday preferred.
  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills and discretion with confidential employee data.

Nice to have:

  • SOX-controlled or public-company experience.
  • Multi-entity or international payroll accounting.
  • Experience with NetSuite, FloQast or payroll-to-GL integrations.
  • CPA, CPP, FPC or comparable credential.

Benefits

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

  • Competitive salary and equity packages
  • Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
  • An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
  • 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
  • Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Region 1 $150,000 - $177,000

Region 2 $130,000 - $153,000

Region 3 $117,000 - $138,000

A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

description:
National Accounts Director – Commercial Fleet Battery Solutions

Lead the Transition from Lead-Acid to Sodium-Ion

About Our Client:

CSI is a fast-growing battery technology company and market leading provider of transportable Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), high-quality advanced battery systems for commercial electric vehicles, and low voltage batteries and electrification components to the North American commercial vehicle market. The company is focused on delivering next-generation 12V battery solutions to the commercial transportation industry. Our portfolio includes new innovative sodium-ion technology designed to improve fleet reliability, safety, sustainability, and total cost of ownership.

The Opportunity

The National Accounts Director will be responsible for developing and managing strategic relationships with the largest truck fleets, leasing companies, fleet maintenance organizations, OEMs, dealer networks, and transportation providers throughout North America. You will play a key role in introducing sodium-ion technology to a market historically dominated by lead-acid batteries while simultaneously growing established battery business across major fleet customers.

This is not a territory sales role. This is a strategic business development position focused on creating long-term enterprise partnerships with the most influential fleets in the industry.

The Ideal Candidate

We are seeking an industry veteran with established commercial fleet relationships and a proven track record in the lead-acid battery industry, selling battery, aftermarket, maintenance, or transportation solutions to the largest fleets in North America. The ideal candidate brings an existing book of business, deep knowledge of traditional battery technologies, and the ability to successfully transition customers to next-generation solutions.

This role requires someone who can effectively articulate the total cost of ownership (TCO) advantages of CSI's innovative 12V Sodium-Ion battery technology, helping customers understand the long-term operational, financial, and sustainability benefits of adopting this emerging technology.

Preferred Industry Experience: We are particularly interested in candidates with experience working for leading battery manufacturers or distributors, including Clarios, East Penn Manufacturing, EnerSys, Exide Technologies, C&D Technologies, Continental Battery Systems, Interstate Batteries, or similar organizations within the lead-acid battery industry.

This is a rare opportunity to help define an emerging battery category while leveraging existing relationships across the trucking and transportation industry.

What Makes This Opportunity Unique

Most battery sales roles focus on defending existing business. This role is about shaping the future of commercial fleet energy storage.

You will have the opportunity to leverage your existing fleet relationships to introduce one of the most promising alternatives to traditional lead-acid batteries while helping fleets reduce maintenance costs, improve reliability, and prepare for the next generation of vehicle electrification.

Key Responsibilities

•Develop executive-level relationships within major transportation fleets and leasing organizations.

•Drive adoption of both lead-acid and sodium-ion battery solutions.

•Secure national supply agreements and multi-year strategic partnerships.

•Build relationships with fleet maintenance, procurement, engineering, operations, sustainability, and executive leadership teams.

•Identify opportunities to improve fleet uptime, battery reliability, maintenance costs, and operational efficiency.

•Collaborate with distributors, truck dealers, service networks, and channel partners.

•Lead strategic account planning and executive business reviews.

•Represent the company at major industry events including:

  • American Trucking Associations (ATA)
  • Technology & Maintenance Council (TMC)
  • National Private Truck Council (NPTC)
  • Heavy Duty Aftermarket Week (HDAW)
  • Fleet and transportation industry conferences

•Provide market intelligence and customer feedback to executive leadership.

Required Experience

•10+ years of national account sales experience.

•Demonstrated success selling into commercial transportation and fleet markets.

•Existing relationships with major fleet organizations.

•Experience negotiating national contracts and enterprise agreements.

•History of exceeding sales targets and building long-term customer partnerships.

•Ability to work independently in a high-growth environment.

Highly Desired Experience

Direct experience with the following:

  • Lead-acid batteries
  • Commercial vehicle batteries
  • Fleet maintenance products
  • Heavy-duty aftermarket parts
  • Commercial vehicle electrical systems
  • Transportation technology
  • Fleet telematics
  • Truck leasing and maintenance programs

Location

•Remote within the United States with significant travel (40%) to customer sites, industry events, and strategic partner meetings.

Compensation & Benefits:

Compensation: $150,000-$200,000/ year commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location, plus uncapped commission

Benefits include:

•Medical, dental, and vision insurance

•401(k) with company matching

•Paid time off and holidays

Join us in transforming how critical infrastructure is powered by accelerating the adoption of clean, flexible, and resilient mobile energy storage solutions.

Salary: $150,000 – $200,000 / year

description:
Job Title: 340B Implementation Quality Assurance Analyst

Location: Remote
Vertical / Department: Customer Engagement / Implementation & Onboarding

Reports To: Implementation Manager
Job Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Position Summary:

A 340B Implementation Quality Assurance (QA) Analyst ensures that a covered entity’s 340B Drug Discount Program is implemented, operated, and maintained in full compliance with HRSA regulations, internal policies, and program integrity standards. This role blends compliance oversight, process implementation, and quality assurance to ensure the 340B program delivers intended savings and meets all regulatory and internal standards. The role is to oversee the implementation, monitoring, and compliance of the 340B program, including audit activities, process validation, and risk mitigation to prevent duplicate discounts, diversion, and eligibility errors.

Program Compliance & Auditing:

  • Conduct regular internal audits of 340B Office of Pharmacy Affairs Information System (OPAIS) records, retail pharmacies (entity-owned and contract), and Medicaid claims to ensure adherence to HRSA requirements
  • Validate patient, provider, and drug eligibility for all 340B transactions
  • Review and interpret state Medicaid billing requirements and compare against claims data
  • Participate in external 340B program audits and prepare data/documentation for review

Implementation & Process Oversight:

  • Develop and maintain 340B policies, procedures, and workflows for purchasing, referral capture, and contract pharmacy management
  • Administer referral prescription capture processes and ensure documentation supports eligibility
  • Monitor contract pharmacy portals for missed claims, investigate denials/reversals, and coordinate remediation
  • Configure and maintain eligible provider tables, location/site mapping, and excluded NDCs/drugs in compliance with internal and HRSA standards

Quality Assurance & Risk Management:

  • Identify compliance risks, prevent diversion, and ensure consistent processes across all points of service
  • Develop training programs (e.g., 340B University OnDemand) for staff on 340B procedures and inventory management
  • Monitor regulatory updates and communicate implications to program operations

Reporting & Collaboration:

  • Generate program utilization, savings, and exception reports for management and stakeholders
  • Collaborate with IT, audit, accounting, and pharmacy teams to share data, improve efficiency, and ensure compliance
  • Provide data, reports, and insights to support other business units

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma/GED; pharmacy or healthcare-related degree preferred
  • 1–3+ years in 340B program work; prior QA, compliance, or pharmacy operations experience preferred

· In-depth knowledge of HRSA 340B regulations and program mechanics

· Proficiency in Excel, SQL, data analysis, and 340B software

· Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills

· Ability to work independently and meet deadlines

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Implementation quality scores.
  • Number of post-go-live defects identified.
  • Defect resolution turnaround times.
  • First-pass testing success rates.
  • Accuracy of implementation validations.
  • Compliance audit findings.
  • Client implementation satisfaction scores.
  • On-time project delivery support.
  • Reduction in implementation rework.
  • Effectiveness of risk identification and mitigation.

What We Offer:

· Health insurance

· Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

· Dental and Vision insurance

· 401(k) retirement plan

· Paid time off

Why Join Pillr Health?

As a leading 340B Third-Party Administrator, we help covered entities maximize program compliance, improve patient access to care, and strengthen healthcare outcomes.

Our Mission:

6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

About the Role:

Are you a compensation leader who loves turning market data into smart, fair pay decisions? 6sense's Total Rewards team is looking for a Compensation Manager to design, govern and evolve our global compensation programs, so our pay and equity practices stay competitive, compliant and aligned with our business goals. You will own core compensation programs and cycles, strengthen job architecture and governance, and use technology, analytics, and AI to make compensation work faster, more consistent, and more actionable.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead the design, implementation, and governance of 6sense's global compensation programs, policies, philosophy and operating standards in partnership, with the Senior Director, Total Rewards
  • Own global salary and equity structures, job architecture, leveling, job codes, and title governance, using market data and internal equity to maintain competitive and consistent frameworks. 
  • Set the compensation and benchmarking, including vendor participation, market-pricing methodology, and regular refreshes of salary and equity bands.
  • Lead and execute the annual and mid-year salary review programs, including salary budget planning, merit guidelines and approvals
  • Build the equity grant budget and model scenarios for compensation strategy proposals
  • Analyze compensation cycle outcomes against philosophy and budget, and present findings and recommendations to leadership
  • Maintenance and day-to-day administration of our equity programs and equity reporting tools
  • Advise People Business Partners, Recruiting, FP&A and business leaders on benchmarks and offers for senior and strategic hires, and handle escalations and exceptions
  • Translate compensation data into clear recommendations, executive dashboards, and quarterly reporting that enable timely, consistent decisions. Ensure compensation programs comply with applicable federal, state, and international requirements, and establish controls that support audit readiness and responsible governance. 
  • Establish compensation governance standards and evaluate program effectiveness to identify areas for improvement
  • Manage compensation vendor relationships, oversee contract timelines and evaluate tool effectiveness ahead of renewals
  • Define requirements and data standards for our compensation planning tools (Workday, Pave and Radford), and approve configuration changes
  • Apply strong AI fluency to redesign compensation workflows, improve analysis and data quality, accelerate scenario modeling and communications, and introduce responsible automation with appropriate human judgment, privacy, and controls. 
  • Propose and create training for employees and managers around our compensation and leveling needs.

What You’ll Bring (Required):

  • 8+ years of experience in compensation, including ownership of equity and sales compensation
  • Demonstrated experience leading compensation cycles, market pricing, job architecture, leveling, pay structures, equity modeling, and executive-ready analysis. 
  • International compensation experience, with working knowledge of compensation practices and regulations across multiple countries
  • Hands-on experience with Workday and compensation tools such as Pave and Radford, along with advanced spreadsheet and data-analysis skills. 
  • Advanced Excel skills (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, dynamic sheets)
  • Strong AI fluency: the ability to select and use AI tools effectively, validate outputs, protect sensitive employee data, and translate AI capabilities into responsible, scalable compensation workflows. 
  • Excellent analytical judgment and communication skills, with the ability to turn complex data into a clear point of view and influence senior stakeholders. 
  • A strategic and solutions-oriented mindset, paired with the willingness to stay close to execution, move with urgency, and bring forward practical recommendations. 

Success in the First 12 Months:

  • Improve overall data quality, reporting consistency, and system governance for compensation, equity, leveling, and salary bands.
  • Modernize executive workforce reporting and self-service analytics capabilities.
  • Streamline and automate key Compensation processes to improve efficiency and our business partnership.
  • Introduce practical AI-enabled solutions that improve the effectiveness of the Compensation function.
  • Build a scalable foundation for future growth through technology, analytics, and operational excellence.

description:
What You'll Do

The Principal Compensation Partner, is a global, director-level individual contributor and a principal compensation subject matter expert for Avalara, supporting the Sales organization. This role sets the direction for global compensation strategy and designs the programs that bring it to life, with a particular focus on the compensation and incentive programs that drive GTM performance. The Principal Compensation Partner turns complex data into clear, compelling narratives that guide decisions, advising executives and senior leaders on the company’s most complex, sensitive, and high-impact compensation matters. This role ensures global compensation programs are competitive, equitable, compliant, and aligned with business strategy and talent objectives. This role operates with a high degree of independence, leads through influence rather than direct authority, and shapes compensation practices across the entire enterprise.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Use analysis and storytelling to drive decisions: turn complex compensation, market, and business data into clear, compelling narratives and executive-ready recommendations that shape decisions by senior leaders
  • Serve as the lead compensation partner and trusted advisor to the Sales organization, advising Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Sales Operations leaders on pay strategy, role structure, and talent attraction and retention for GTM roles.
  • Partner with GTM, Finance, and Sales Operations on the design, governance, and annual refresh of sales incentive programs, including pay mix, on-target earnings, quota and commission structures, and plan performance, ensuring they motivate the right behaviors and align with business goals.
  • Drive global compensation strategy and philosophy in partnership with People leadership, ensuring programs support business strategy, talent attraction and retention, and financial objectives, with a focus in the Sales organization.
  • Own and evolve Avalara’s sales job architecture framework and leveling governance, setting standards for job evaluation, EEO and FLSA classification, and internal equity, and making final determinations on the most complex and precedent-setting leveling decisions.
  • Partner with Finance on sales compensation budgeting, forecasting, and cost modeling, using advanced scenario analysis to evaluate the financial and talent impact of program decisions, including the cost and return of GTM incentive investments.
  • Conduct advanced compensation analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and present findings with clear insight, a point of view, and a recommended course of action.
  • Lead and influence cross-functional, enterprise-wide initiatives by building alignment among senior stakeholders, managing risk, and driving measurable business outcomes.
  • Coach, mentor, and develop compensation team members and other senior individual contributors, setting standards for quality, analytical rigor, and storytelling, and sharing expertise across the People organization.
  • Optimizes AI tools used across compensation, and apply them to improve insight generation, compensation modeling, and executive reporting.

What You'll Need to be Successful

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive compensation experience, including within a technology company.
  • Significant experience supporting a sales or go-to-market organization, including sales compensation or incentive plan design and administration.
  • Extensive experience designing and leading global compensation programs in a complex, multi-region environment.
  • Proven experience advising executives and senior leaders on complex, high-stakes compensation decisions.
  • Demonstrated track record of using data analysis and storytelling to influence senior-level decisions.
  • Experience leading large-scale, cross-functional initiatives with measurable business impact.
  • Experience coaching and developing compensation professionals.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI tools to enhance data analysis, reporting, modeling, or process efficiency.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Exceptional analytical and data storytelling skills, with the ability to distill complex data into clear narratives and visuals that drive decisions.
  • Expert knowledge of compensation principles, job architecture, market pricing methodologies, and incentive and equity program design.
  • Strong understanding of sales compensation principles, including pay mix, quota setting, commission and accelerator structures, and the link between incentives and sales performance.
  • Deep experience conducting market benchmarking using survey providers such as Radford, Mercer, and WTW, including strong command of survey methodology and data strategy.
  • Experience using Workday or similar Human Capital Management systems.
  • Advanced Excel skills, including modeling, scenario analysis, and executive-level reporting.
  • Strategic thinking and strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate business needs and frame recommendations in terms of business impact.
  • Knowledge of global compensation regulations and emerging legislative trends, including pay transparency and pay equity requirements.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion in highly ambiguous, sensitive, and high-impact situations.
  • Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to build credibility with senior leaders and influence without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) designation.
  • Experience supporting compensation programs in a public company environment, including exposure to executive compensation and Compensation Committee processes.
  • Experience in a high-growth or technology company, particularly a SaaS or subscription-based business.
  • Experience partnering with Sales Operations and Finance on sales incentive plan design and analytics.
  • Experience leading global compensation program design and structure, including through M&A integration or organizational change.
  • Experience conducting pay equity analysis and regulatory reporting.
  • Advanced degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, or a related field.

AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.

  • You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.

  • You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.

Total Rewards

Inclusive culture and diversity Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. We also have a total of 8 employee-run resource groups, each with senior leadership and exec sponsorship.

We’re defining the relationship between tax and tech.

We’ve already built an industry-leading cloud compliance platform, processing over 54 billion customer API calls and over 6.6 million tax returns a year. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.

Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

When a customer pushes a change, they need their CI/CD jobs to start quickly and run reliably, even when demand spikes. You'll help make that happen on GitLab.com by improving how Hosted Runners provision compute, isolate customer workloads, and recover from failures. Your decisions will shape how long customers wait for jobs to start and how efficiently GitLab uses cloud compute.

As a Senior Staff Site Reliability Engineer, you'll set technical direction across teams while continuing to write and operate production software in Go. You'll lead work across the runner control plane, worker provisioning, and job execution. Your primary focus will be GitLab.com, and you'll also provide technical leadership support for GitLab Dedicated Hosted Runners. You'll report to the engineering manager responsible for Hosted Runners.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Tuning autoscaling to reduce job wait times during demand spikes
  • Evaluating ways to isolate customer workloads
  • Improving how runner usage is measured for capacity planning and billing

What You'll Do

  • Lead architecture and delivery across teams. Plan migrations with representative workload tests, safe capacity handovers, and rollback paths.
  • Write, review, and ship Go code across GitLab Runner, autoscaling components, cloud integrations, and operational tooling.
  • Improve reliability from job pickup through cleanup. Join the Runners Platform on-call rotation, investigate failures across system layers, and verify fixes in production.
  • Work with Security and Runner engineers to evaluate workload isolation, balancing security and compatibility with performance and cost.
  • Build observability that connects the customer experience with fleet behavior and guides capacity decisions. Partner with Finance, Product, and the billing platform team on usage metering and cost attribution.
  • Reduce recurring operational work through automation, tooling, and runbooks that engineers can use independently.
  • Mentor experienced engineers through design, implementation, and operations. Clarify ownership across teams and help engineers validate AI-assisted changes before they reach production.

What You'll Bring

  • Recent hands-on experience building and operating production systems software such as controllers, agents, or schedulers. You've personally shipped code that handles challenges such as concurrency, retries, or resource cleanup.
  • Strong programming skills in Go or another systems language, with the ability to become productive in Go.
  • Deep Linux and networking knowledge. You can trace production failures across system layers and use measurements to validate fixes.
  • Experience operating Kubernetes in production, including diagnosing scheduling and resource issues and managing rollouts and recovery.
  • Experience building or operating autoscaled or dynamically scheduled compute, such as VM fleets, serverless platforms, or batch systems. You bring experience with public cloud and infrastructure automation or comparable fleet operations.
  • A working understanding of the CI job lifecycle and the implications of running customer-controlled code. You can bring that knowledge from outside a CI/CD team.
  • A record of leading technical initiatives across teams and personally contributing to implementation through production. You build agreement through clear writing and asynchronous collaboration, and mentor engineers to own what they build and operate.

About the team

Hosted Runners operates the compute behind customers' CI/CD jobs. You'll work with Runner Core to turn lessons from operating the fleet into improvements to the open-source GitLab Runner. You'll also work with Product and partner teams to agree on priorities and ownership for shared changes.

Senior Manager, Support Engineering (U.S. Government)

An overview of this role

As a Senior Manager, Support Engineering on our U.S. Government support team, you’ll co-lead a team of engineers supporting complex enterprise deployments in highly regulated environments. You’ll combine people-focused leadership, technical judgment, and business acumen to develop engineers, strengthen our support program, and help customers realize value from GitLab.

You’ll also connect the team’s technical contributions to outcomes that matter across the business. This includes telling a compelling, evidence-based story about how Support Engineering helps protect revenue, enable growth, remove barriers to adoption, and accelerate customer time to value. You’ll help executives and sales teams understand the significance of the work engineers perform and how that work supports customer and organizational success.

Beyond individual cases, you’ll recognize Support Engineering as a valuable source of business intelligence. By bringing together engineers’ firsthand observations, product trends, and recurring customer pain points, you’ll turn field signal into actionable insights for Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success.

What you’ll do

  • Co-lead, coach, and develop a team of Support Engineers, building a culture of trust, accountability, technical excellence, and customer-focused decision-making.
  • Drive hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career development, helping engineers build technical expertise, communication skills, and an understanding of their broader business impact.
  • Partner with other Support Engineering Managers to shape program strategy, establish priorities, plan capacity, and evolve processes and tooling as customer and business needs change.
  • Translate complex technical work into clear, compelling narratives for executives and sales teams, connecting engineers’ contributions to revenue protection, growth opportunities, customer adoption, and faster time to value.
  • Use operational data, customer context, and qualitative feedback to evaluate support effectiveness, communicate impact, and guide investment and improvement decisions.
  • Establish a repeatable approach to capturing engineers’ insights and identifying product trends, recurring customer pain points, adoption barriers, and emerging government requirements.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success to turn support intelligence into actionable recommendations for product improvements, enablement, and customer engagement.
  • Maintain technical engagement by joining customer calls, reviewing tickets, and helping engineers navigate complex or sensitive issues, while developing the team’s ability to resolve challenges independently.
  • Coordinate responses to escalated and critical customer situations during working hours, providing clear communication and sound judgment.
  • Champion improvements that address recurring problems, reduce customer friction, and strengthen the quality and scalability of our U.S. Government support offering.

What you’ll bring

  • Demonstrated success leading and developing technical support or engineering teams, including coaching, performance management, career development, and leadership through growth and change.
  • A strong technical background supporting complex enterprise software or infrastructure, with the ability to assess technical challenges, recognize the value engineers deliver, and understand the implications for customer outcomes.
  • Experience translating technical accomplishments into business value for executive and sales audiences, using clear storytelling supported by data and customer context.
  • Business acumen to connect support outcomes with revenue protection, customer retention, growth, product adoption, and time to value.
  • The ability to treat engineers’ knowledge and customer interactions as sources of business intelligence, synthesizing individual observations into meaningful trends and actionable recommendations.
  • Experience setting priorities, planning resources, and improving support programs while balancing immediate customer needs with longer-term organizational goals.
  • A people-focused leadership approach that builds trust, encourages candid feedback, recognizes contributions, and creates opportunities for engineers to grow.
  • Experience managing high-severity incidents and sensitive escalations, including effective communication with customers, executives, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • The ability to influence across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success, building alignment around customer needs and shared business outcomes.
  • Familiarity with U.S. Government customers and the operational, security, and regulatory constraints that shape their environments. We also welcome candidates with relevant experience in other complex or regulated industries.

About the team

Our U.S. Government Support team formed in 2019 and has grown alongside the adoption of GitLab within government agencies. We help customers troubleshoot complex environments and use GitLab’s DevSecOps platform securely and effectively.

Distributed across the United States, we combine synchronous and asynchronous collaboration to support customers and build strong working relationships in a remote-first environment. Our team includes both tenured and newer engineers, bringing diverse technical experience and perspectives.

We’re focused on developing our people, scaling our operations, strengthening crisis management for sensitive systems, and deepening our partnerships across GitLab. As a senior leader, you’ll help make the team’s technical expertise and customer knowledge more valuable to the broader organization, while ensuring engineers have the support, direction, and development opportunities they need to succeed.

excerpt: Overview Millennium is proud to be part of the Markon enterprise, a network of specialized organizations united in support of critical national security missions.
description:
Overview

Millennium is proud to be part of the Markon enterprise, a network of specialized organizations united in support of critical national security missions. This partnership strengthens our ability to deliver results by expanding our technical depth, operational reach, and access to a broader bench of proven experts, ensuring our customers continue to receive best-in-class cybersecurity support.Since 2004, Millennium has operated at the forefront of cybersecurity. Our elite team of over 300 professionals brings an unmatched record of performance across Red Team Operations, Defensive Cyber Operations, Software Engineering, and Technical Engineering. As home to the largest contingent of contracted Red Team operators supporting the Department of Defense, Millennium delivers unparalleled threat intelligence and battle-tested expertise to both DoD and federal civilian customers.

What We Believe

Millennium is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate or allow discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, citizenship, disability, veteran status or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law.

Responsibilities

Millennium Corporation is seeking a Cyber Security Engineer III to support cybersecurity, software assurance, and security engineering activities within a DoD/DoN environment. This position is 100% remote and will focus on integrating cybersecurity throughout the software development and delivery lifecycle, with an emphasis on application security, CI/CD pipeline security, container security, vulnerability management, and DoD cybersecurity compliance.

Candidates located in or near major U.S. Navy installations are preferred, with priority given to candidates in the New Orleans, Orlando, and Washington, DC metropolitan areas. Candidates located near other major Navy facilities may also be considered.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct code and container vulnerability assessments using approved DoD vulnerability scanning tools, DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), Security Requirements Guides (SRGs), and other DoD/DoN software assurance tools.
  • Implement and assess operating system security configurations in accordance with applicable DISA STIGs and SRGs.
  • Perform cybersecurity assessments, security audits, and risk analyses to identify vulnerabilities and compliance gaps.
  • Apply security testing methodologies, including Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Review and implement cybersecurity policies and security controls within CI/CD pipelines to support secure software delivery and DoD/DoN requirements.
  • Serve as a GitLab security reviewer and approver for merge requests, reviewing security scan results and verifying that identified findings are remediated or appropriately documented through the approved risk-management process prior to release.
  • Review GitLab SAST, dependency, secret detection, and container scanning results; coordinate remediation activities with development teams and track findings through closure.
  • Review changes to GitLab security policies, pipeline controls, and protected branch settings to ensure required security checks and approvals remain properly enforced.
  • Provide cybersecurity oversight for containerized workloads using NeuVector, including review of vulnerability findings, admission control decisions, and runtime security alerts.
  • Collaborate with application and platform teams to investigate NeuVector findings, tune security policies, and document remediation actions or accepted risks.
  • Ensure security-related provisions within system acquisition and program documentation address identified cybersecurity requirements.
  • Provide cybersecurity guidance and assist with developing mitigation strategies for DoD information systems.
  • Prepare Risk Management Framework (RMF) artifacts and Memoranda of Agreement (MoAs) with system owners supporting interface and networking implementations.
  • Identify and evaluate Common Criteria and National Information Assurance Partnership (NIAP) certified technologies when applicable.
  • Evaluate cybersecurity products and technologies used by programs to validate compliance with applicable DoD/DoN requirements.
  • Support cybersecurity activities across the software lifecycle and collaborate with engineering, development, platform, and program teams to address security requirements and risks.

Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance.
  • Bachelor's degree with 8 years of relevant experience, or a high school diploma/equivalent with 13 years of relevant experience.
  • Experience working within the DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) and familiarity with DoDI 8510.01.
  • An Information Assurance Manager (IAM) Level II certification in accordance with DoD 8570.01-M, such as:-CISSP-GSLC-CISM
  • Experience with DoD cybersecurity requirements, including DISA STIGs and SRGs.
  • Experience with software security testing methodologies, including SAST and DAST.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity within CI/CD or DevSecOps environments.
  • Experience with GitLab security tools and processes, including reviewing security scan results and supporting vulnerability remediation.
  • Candidates should be located in or near a major U.S. Navy installation. Preferred locations include New Orleans, LA; Orlando, FL; and the Washington, DC metropolitan area. Candidates near other major Navy facilities may also be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency with GitLab, NeuVector, and Sonatype.
  • Experience with container security and vulnerability management.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity within a DoD or Department of the Navy (DoN) environment.
  • Experience with the Navy's Rapid Assess and Incorporate Software Engineering (RAISE) methodology.
  • Experience with the RAISE Platform of Choice (RPOC).
  • Experience evaluating Common Criteria and NIAP-certified technologies.
  • Experience developing or supporting RMF artifacts, security documentation, and cybersecurity mitigation strategies.

Business Development

Assist with Business Development activities as required to support Millennium's strategic business objectives, which may include but not limited to participation in technical interviews, creation of technical documentation, general proposal writing support and proposal color reviews.

Physical Requirements

  • Must be comfortable with prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Must be able to lift up to 10-15 pounds at a time.

COMPENSATION:

$125,000- $135,000

The salary range provided for this position is intended as a general guideline and does not guarantee a specific salary or compensation amount. Final compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including, relevant education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities

description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring a Senior Backend Software Engineer to join our Identity Experience (IDX) team in Brazil! This is a Remote – Brazil position, meaning you can work from anywhere within the country. Please note that this role is only open to candidates in Brazil.

We’re looking for an autonomous and resourceful Senior Software Engineer to join our international Identity Experience (IDX) team. The IDX team owns critical services at the heart of our product, including account creation, account management, account recovery, permissions management, and more.

In this role, you’ll build features that sit at the spine of the product and power experiences used by millions of users. You’ll tackle complex engineering challenges where performance, reliability, and scalability are essential, while designing and evolving systems built to operate at massive scale.

You’ll also play a key role in driving our AI transformation, leveraging your experience with AI-assisted development to raise engineering standards, accelerate delivery, and build seamless, reliable identity experiences.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Drive and own critical core identity services, including account creation, account management, permissions management, and account recovery.
  • Architect and build scalable, highly resilient backend systems to support global user growth.
  • Optimize system performance and infrastructure efficiency across core microservices.
  • Develop high-impact new products and features with a high degree of autonomy and resourcefulness.
  • Lead AI transformation within the team by leveraging AI-assisted development practices to elevate engineering standards.
  • Collaborate closely with international cross-functional teams, UX, and product leadership to deliver seamless identity experiences.
  • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life balance

WHO YOU ARE

  • You have experience building and operating backend systems in production environments. Golang expertise is highly desirable.
  • You have strong experience with distributed systems, APIs, data-intensive applications, large-scale cloud-native architectures and scalable databases such as PostgreSQL, with experience designing and scaling systems on platforms such as Google Cloud Platform or AWS.
  • You have hands-on experience with Kubernetes or similar container orchestration platforms, including deploying, scaling, and operating services in production.
  • You can independently own projects end-to-end, from technical design through implementation and operation, while collaborating effectively with engineers across teams.
  • You care deeply about maintainable, reliable code, make thoughtful technical decisions, and continuously look for ways to improve production systems.
  • You communicate clearly and confidently, and are comfortable driving technical discussions, influencing decisions, and sharing ideas across teams.
  • You have a high level of AI fluency and thoughtfully leverage modern tools, including LLMs and AI-assisted development, to improve engineering workflows and problem-solving.
  • We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that prior experience in building and operating distributed backend systems at scale is a mandatory requirement.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life.

Our flexible benefits program allows you to customize some of the benefits, according to your needs!

Our benefits include:

WELLHUB: Free Gold+ membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

WELLZ: A complete emotional wellbeing program with a unique approach. It offers personalized journeys that combine individual therapy sessions (52 per year) and on-demand content.

HEALTHCARE: Health, dental, and life insurance.

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. When you join, use our home office reimbursement to set up your home office.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE: Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: It’s important to take time away from work to recharge.Employees receive vacations after 6 months and additional 3 days off per year + 1 day off for each year of tenure (up to 5 additional days) + an extra holiday for your birthday!

PAID PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions, build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success.

CULTURE: You’ll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. excerpt: About Conduit Conduit is an AI agent platform built for hospitality.
description:
About Conduit

Conduit is an AI agent platform built for hospitality. Hotels, vacation rentals, and resorts use our agents for guest communication and internal operations, and those agents run millions of workflows a day.

Hospitality is 10% of global GDP, and guests judge it by how fast their requests get resolved. Resolving one usually means working across several tools and several people. Our agents do that coordination.

Role: Agent Strategy Manager

Some of our customers are property managers with no tech team. They hand us their guest support and operations, and we run them. Our agents do the work, and a remote team of virtual assistants picks up what the agents can't handle yet.

You own those customers after launch. You are the person they talk to every week, and you make sure they get more out of Conduit every month. You work as a pair with an Agent Deployment Strategist, who builds and tunes the agents. You own the relationship, the results the customer sees, and what we take on for them next.

Why this role is different

  • This is not a classic customer success role. You work in the product yourself: you read real guest conversations, find where the agent went wrong, and make the small fixes on our platform without waiting on anyone.

  • You own numbers, not just relationships: automation rate, guest outcomes, and how much more each customer runs on Conduit.

  • You help decide what we build next. Once we run a customer's guest support, we can take on dynamic pricing, getting their properties found in AI search answers, and accounting. You see which of these each customer needs first.

What the work looks like

  • Weekly check-ins with each customer on what the agents handled, what changed, and what comes next.

  • Turning customer feedback into agent changes, making the small ones yourself and scoping the bigger ones with your Agent Deployment Strategist.

  • Working with our Customer Ops team when something goes wrong, and making sure it doesn't happen twice.

  • Spotting where a customer can do more with us, and bringing in our sales team for the commercial side.

  • Writing down what works so every customer gets the same playbook.

Who you are

  • 3+ years in customer success, account management, technical account management, or implementation at a software or AI company. No hospitality background needed.

  • You have gone hands-on in the product you supported, not only managed the relationship.

  • You measure. You can tell us how you knew a customer was getting value, and what you did when they weren't.

  • You like operators and the people doing the work, and they trust you.

  • This role can be remote in the US, or in our San Francisco office. Candidates must be authorized to work in the US; we do not sponsor visas.

Compensation and Benefits

  • $100-180K base

  • 0.05%-0.15% equity

  • Performance bonus

  • Comprehensive health insurance and 401k match

  • Dinner covered every day

Interview Process

  • Intro call with the founders

  • Customer case with the founders: a customer is unhappy with what the agent did last week, and you work out what happened and what to tell them

  • Final round (onsite in San Francisco or virtual)

  • Culture fit conversation with the founders

title: Research Engineering Manager, STEM
excerpt: About Turing Turing’s mission is to accelerate superintelligence to drive real economic progress.
description:
About Turing

Turing’s mission is to accelerate superintelligence to drive real economic progress. Headquartered in San Francisco, Turing works with frontier AI labs to generate high-quality datasets, reinforcement learning environments, and frontier research benchmarks that improve model capabilities in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and advanced STEM reasoning. In software engineering, Turing is the largest and longest-running data provider in the category. Turing also works with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, life sciences, healthcare, retail, automotive, and CPG to build and deploy end-to-end agentic AI systems inside mission-critical workflows. By operating on both sides, Turing closes the loop between frontier research and enterprise deployment, turning real-world deployment signals into better data, evaluations, and more capable models. Learn more at .

The Role

Turing builds large-scale datasets and reinforcement learning (RL) environments that power post-training for the world's leading AI labs and enterprises.

The STEM Horizontal team produces the high-signal coding and STEM data frontier labs train on. We're looking for a Research Engineering Manager to lead the research engineering behind its next layer: synthetic data that measurably improves models, and new benchmarks that measure what today's evals miss.

You'll lead a team of research engineers, work side by side with research scientists, and stay close enough to the code to review an eval harness line by line or prototype a generator yourself when the team needs it. You'll also build the team: hiring research engineers is a core part of this role, not a side task. Ideally you've been on the other side, at a frontier lab, and know what makes a lab trust a dataset or a benchmark result.

  • Synthetic data that earns its place. Generation, verification, and filtering pipelines where every sample is checked, and where we can show which properties of the data drive downstream gains, not just how much of it we made.
  • Benchmarks that stay meaningful. New evaluations for capabilities current benchmarks miss, built with calibrated difficulty, contamination controls, and statistics strong enough that a lab can make a decision on the result.

Quality failures here are quiet. A subtle bug in a verifier doesn't crash anything; it ships thousands of wrong labels into someone's training run and costs weeks. If you want to build the team and the systems that catch that early, this is the seat.

What You'll Do

1. Build and Lead the Team

  • Build the team: define the profiles you need, run hiring, and grow research engineers selected for research taste as much as engineering rigor.
  • Run the team's operating rhythm: project selection, planning, experiment reviews, design docs, and clear ownership.
  • Coach engineers on experimental design, code quality, and presenting results; give direct, regular feedback and run fair performance cycles.
  • Define the standards the team works to: eval methodology, data quality bars, and reproducibility — every dataset and result can be regenerated from a commit, a config, and a seed.

2. Partner with Research Scientists

  • Turn hypotheses into experiment plans together: what we're testing, the baseline, the ablations, and the result that would change our minds.
  • Set the agenda with research scientists. You're expected to bring your own hypotheses, not only implement theirs.
  • Take research prototypes to production scale without losing the scientific intent.

3. Build Synthetic Data Systems at Scale

  • Own synthetic data pipelines that generate, verify, filter, deduplicate, and version data, combining programmatic generators, LLM-based generation, automated verifiers, and targeted expert review.
  • Judge data by its effect on models: ablations and fine-tuning or RL experiments that show which attributes (difficulty, diversity, correctness, coverage) drive gains.
  • Build quality systems that hold up at volume: gold sets, LLM-judge calibration against expert labels, sampling audits, and agreement metrics.

4. Create New Benchmarks and Evaluations

  • Find where frontier models fail and where existing benchmarks have saturated, and design evaluations that measure what's missing.
  • Own benchmark methodology end to end: task taxonomy, difficulty calibration, graders and verifiers, contamination controls, held-out splits, and confidence intervals.
  • Ship eval harnesses, including agentic and sandboxed-execution evals, that are deterministic, reproducible, and trusted by internal teams and partner labs.
  • Make the call on whether a result holds up: partner labs and internal teams act on your sign-off.
  • Publish benchmarks, datasets, and findings with our research scientists at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR.

5. Stay Hands-On and Work with Frontier Labs

  • Write code every week on the hardest, highest-leverage parts: core verifier logic, eval statistics, the pipeline component everything else depends on. Expect a third or more of your time on direct technical work.
  • Be the person the team brings its hardest debugging and methodology questions to: why a judge disagrees with experts, why an eval number moved, whether a gain is real or noise.
  • Act as a technical counterpart to researchers at frontier AI labs: scope requests, set acceptance criteria, and explain results and trade-offs plainly.
  • Partner with Strategic Project Leads, delivery, and engineering teams so research advances land in client work and in the platforms the team builds.

Sample Projects

  • Identify a capability gap, design and ship a benchmark for it, and see it adopted by partner labs.
  • Stand up a synthetic data pipeline for long-horizon coding tasks with execution-based verifiers, and run the ablations that show which task properties drive RL gains.
  • Calibrate an LLM-judge grading system against expert labels, map where it fails, and decide where humans stay in the loop.
  • Design the experiment that tells a partner lab whether a two-point gain on their eval is real.
  • Decide which of three competing synthetic data approaches the team should bet on, and design the experiments that settle it.

Tech Stack

  • Research: Python · PyTorch or JAX · SFT · DPO · PPO / GRPO · RL with verifiable rewards
  • Evals & data: LLM-as-judge · programmatic verifiers · sandboxed execution · gold sets · contamination checks
  • Platform: Python services (Django / FastAPI) · PostgreSQL · Docker · Terraform · AWS or GCP

What We're Looking For

  • Experience: 8+ years of hands-on ML or research engineering, at least 5 in industry, including 3+ years directly managing research engineers, ML engineers, or researchers (hiring and performance management included).
  • Synthetic data at scale: you've owned synthetic or curated data pipelines in production whose output drove training decisions, and can show how you measured their quality and downstream impact.
  • Evaluation rigor: you've designed and shipped LLM evals or benchmarks that others used to make model decisions, and understand contamination, saturation, judge bias, inter-annotator agreement, variance, and confidence intervals.
  • Experimental judgment: you plan ablations up front, choose baselines honestly, and can tell a real effect from noise.
  • Technical depth: strong Python; production experience with PyTorch or JAX; working knowledge of the post-training stack (SFT, DPO, PPO/GRPO, RL with verifiable rewards).
  • Technical direction: a track record of setting direction for a team, not only executing a roadmap handed to you.
  • Scale: distributed data processing and large evaluation or training jobs (e.g., Ray, Spark, Kubernetes) on AWS or GCP.
  • Communication: clear written communication for scientists and non-specialists alike; comfortable presenting results to researchers at partner labs.
  • AI-forward: daily use of LLM coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) as part of how you ship, with the judgment to review their output critically. This is a must-have.
  • Education: PhD or Master's degree in AI, machine learning, computer science, statistics, or a closely related field; PhD preferred. Exceptional equivalent research experience will also be considered. We weigh industry outcomes most heavily.

Strongly Preferred

  • Frontier AI lab experience: post-training data, evals, or reward modeling at a frontier lab (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI) or a top industry research group.
  • Built or contributed to a public benchmark or dataset the community uses.

Nice to Have

  • First-author papers at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or similar.
  • RL environment and verifier design for agentic tasks: coding agents, tool use, computer use, long-horizon workflows.
  • Data valuation or attribution: measuring what each slice of data contributes to a model.
  • Depth in a STEM domain such as math, physics, chemistry, or biology (not required).
  • Experience managing tech leads or managers, or running several concurrent programs.
  • Directing large expert networks through specs, rubrics, and fast feedback loops.

A note from our CTO, Ece Kamar

Some of the most important questions in AI can't be answered from inside a single lab: how to evaluate frontier models, how data and RL truly drive capability, and what happens when AI meets the real world. At Turing, we work directly with frontier labs, the academic community, and enterprises deploying AI at scale. That creates a feedback loop where deployment shapes our research and our research shapes the field, and we publish our findings, datasets, and benchmarks openly. BlackSky is a real-time intelligence company.
